docs.title: Frappe Framework
docs.text:
Frappe Framework is a full-stack web framework in Python and JavaScript. It is metadata driven. You describe data as DocTypes, and Frappe makes the database tables, the REST API, the desk forms, lists and reports, and the permission checks. You put your code in apps. A bench runs many sites, and each site installs a set of apps.

Version: 16 (stable)

These pages describe version 16 (branch version-16-hotfix). Every page was verified against the code of this branch. Other versions: v15 (stable) and develop (unreleased).

docs.title: Start here
docs.text: If you want to Read Install Frappe and make a site Installation Understand how the parts fit Architecture Build a first app Quickstart Look up a term Glossary See what changed since version 15 What's New Move an app from version 15 Upgrading

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• User Guide: use the desk, set up users and permissions, automate work, print, report, publish web pages, and use Flow and Studio.
  • Developer Guide: build apps: DocTypes, controllers, hooks, the database API, REST, background jobs, desk scripts, website pages and tests.
  • Reference: complete lists of hooks, CLI commands, REST endpoints, site config keys, Python and JavaScript APIs, field types and DocTypes.
  • For AI Agents: rules and facts for agents that write or change Frappe apps.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Examples use the app sample_app, the DocTypes Sample Item and Sample Order, the role Sample Role and the user user1@example.com.
  • File paths in frappe/... are relative to the frappe app repository. Paths in sample_app/... are files in your app.
  • Commands run from the bench folder. Replace <site> with your site name.

docs.title: For AI Agents
docs.text: Read this page before you write or change code for a Frappe app on version 16. Every fact here was checked in the version-16-hotfix branch. For an index of all pages with one-line summaries, read llms.txt.

docs.title: Know the version first
docs.text:
1. Run bench version or read frappe/__init__.py __version__. These docs are for 16.x.
  2. Do not use an API from another version without checking it. frappe.read_doc, frappe.enqueue_task, bench enable-app, v2 bulk endpoints and storage v2 do not exist in version 16. extend_doctype_class, Flow, Studio, MCP and the /desk route are new in version 16.

docs.text: Question Page Which hooks exist and what shape they take Hooks reference Run order of controller methods and doc_events Controllers Signatures of frappe.*, frappe.db.*, frappe.utils.* Python API, Database API, Utils Client-side frappe.* and frm API JavaScript API, Form Scripts REST routes REST Endpoints CLI commands and flags CLI Config keys Site Config Field types and DB columns Field Types

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Use frappe.session.user for the current user. frappe.user is None.
  • Check permissions in every whitelisted method. Use doc.check_permission("read") or frappe.has_permission. frappe.get_doc does not check read permission.
  • frappe.get_all ignores permissions. frappe.get_list applies them. Neither has a default row limit in Python. Pass limit. In JavaScript, frappe.db.get_list defaults to 20 rows.
  • frappe.db.set_value, frappe.db.sql and frappe.qb skip validations, controller methods and permissions.
  • frappe.qb.get_query ignores permissions by default (ignore_permissions=True).
  • Write SQL functions in fields in the dict form. A string such as "count(name) as c" raises ValidationError.
  • Do not call frappe.db.commit() in a request handler or a controller method. The request commits when it succeeds, but only for POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE (or when frappe.local.flags.commit is set). Writes in a GET request are rolled back. Inside doc_events handlers transaction control is disabled.
  • A has_permission hook can only deny. Any falsy return value, None included, denies access.
  • Add type annotations to whitelisted methods. Request arguments are validated against them.
  • @frappe.whitelist() takes allow_guest, xss_safe and methods. Without methods, the method accepts GET, POST, PUT and DELETE. Restrict methods that write: @frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"]).
  • The server does not evaluate depends_on, mandatory_depends_on or read_only_depends_on. Only the desk does.
  • Dotted paths in hooks.py fail only when the hook runs. Check that each path imports.
  • override_doctype_class, extend_doctype_class, doctype_js and doctype_list_js do not apply to custom DocTypes (custom = 1).
  • The desk is at /desk. Old /app/... links redirect.

docs.title: Lifecycle order (insert)
docs.text: before_insert → before_naming → autoname → before_validate → validate → before_save → DB insert → after_insert → on_update → on_change. For each step, Frappe runs the controller method, then the doc_events handlers for the DocType, then the "*" handlers. See Controllers for save, submit, cancel, delete and the exact rules.

docs.title: Pitfalls seen in this code base
docs.text:
• require_type_annotated_api_methods is set in frappe's own hooks.py, but no version 16 code reads it.
  • The regex and ilike filters fail on MariaDB.
  • server_script_enabled works only in common_site_config.json.
  • Fixture import deletes and inserts again any record that already exists. Changes made on the site to a fixture record are lost at each bench migrate.
  • A background job that is retried after a deadlock runs as Administrator.
  • frappe.flow.lib.session.new_session() commits. An agent run inside a document event commits in the middle of the save.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: frappe/deprecation_dumpster.py holds deprecated functions. They print a warning and are planned for removal in version 17. Examples: frappe.connect(site=...), the txt argument of frappe.generate_hash, frappe.get_test_records, and the gravatar helpers in frappe.utils.

docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text:
Build and extend Frappe apps: app structure, data model, database, security, APIs, background work, desk UI, website, output, low-code tools, testing and operations.

Topic What it covers Building Apps Create an app, use hooks, extend other apps, ship fixtures and patches, and translate. Data Model Define DocTypes, naming rules, controllers and the document lifecycle, and handle files. Database Read and write data with frappe.db and frappe.qb, and control transactions. Permissions and Security Control access with permissions, authenticate clients and write secure code. APIs Expose whitelisted methods, use the REST API and connect AI clients over MCP. Jobs, Realtime and Caching Run background jobs and scheduled tasks, push realtime events and cache data. Desk UI Script forms and lists, call the server from JavaScript, and build desk pages and navigation. Website and Portal Build website pages, portal pages, routes and web forms. Reports, Printing and Email Write script and query reports, print formats and PDFs, and send email and notifications. Low-Code and AI Use server and client scripts, the automation engine, Flow agents and Studio apps. Testing and Performance Test apps and make them fast. Configuration and Operations Configure sites, deploy to production and upgrade between versions.

docs.title: APIs
docs.text:
Expose whitelisted methods, use the REST API and connect AI clients over MCP.

Page What it covers Whitelisted Methods Expose Python functions over HTTP with @frappe.whitelist, validate arguments with type annotations, restrict access by role, rate limit, and override methods of other apps. REST API Read and change documents and call whitelisted methods over HTTP with /api/v1 (resource, method) and /api/v2 (document, doctype, method), including list parameters, responses and errors. MCP and API Discovery Connect AI agents to a site through the built-in MCP endpoint at /api/v2/mcp, and describe whitelisted methods with the /api/v2/discovery endpoints.

docs.title: MCP and API Discovery
docs.text: Each site has a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at /api/v2/mcp. An AI agent (an MCP client) connects as a desk user and gets tools to search DocTypes, read and write documents, and call whitelisted methods. Every tool goes through the same permission checks as the REST API. The API discovery endpoints at /api/v2/discovery describe the whitelisted methods of the site, with their arguments and docstrings. MCP uses them, and you can call them from any API client.

docs.title: Enable MCP
docs.text:
MCP is on by default. The settings are in System Settings > AI Agents > MCP Settings:

Field Default Description enable_mcp 1 Off: /api/v2/mcp returns HTTP 404. server_name host name Name sent to clients in serverInfo. The default is the host name with other characters changed to _, such as frappe_localhost_8006. agent_instructions empty Text added to the server instructions that agents get when they connect. Tell agents what the site is for.

docs.title: Connect a client
docs.text:
The endpoint uses the Streamable HTTP transport with plain JSON responses. It keeps no protocol session.

  • URL: https://<site>/api/v2/mcp
  • Method: POST only. Other methods get HTTP 405.
  • Headers: Content-Type: application/json, and an Accept that allows application/json.
  • Authentication: any method the REST API accepts: OAuth 2 bearer token, API key and secret (Authorization: token <key>:<secret>), or a session cookie. See Authentication.
  • The user must have the Desk User role. Guests get HTTP 401. Users without the role get HTTP 403.
  • A request with an Origin header from another host must match allow_cors in site config.

Without credentials, the response is HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<site>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource". MCP clients use it to start an OAuth flow. The metadata endpoint is served when OAuth Settings > Show Protected Resource Metadata is on. See Integrations.

Protocol versions: 2025-11-25 (with initialize) and 2026-07-28 (with server/discover and the MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers). A request without MCP-Protocol-Version uses 2025-11-25.

docs.title: Example with curl
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/v2/mcp" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize",
       "params": {"protocolVersion": "2025-11-25", "capabilities": {},
                  "clientInfo": {"name": "sample-client", "version": "1.0"}}}'

{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": {
  "protocolVersion": "2025-11-25",
  "capabilities": {"tools": {"listChanged": false}},
  "serverInfo": {"name": "frappe_localhost_8006", "version": "16.60.2"},
  "instructions": "This is a Frappe Framework site at frappe.localhost:8006.\nYou are connected as Administrator (Administrator).\n..."}}

Call a tool:

curl -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/v2/mcp" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call",
       "params": {"name": "list_documents",
                  "arguments": {"doctype": "Sample Item", "fields": ["name", "rate"],
                                "filters": {"category": "Hardware"}, "limit": 2}}}'

The result has content (JSON as text), structuredContent and isError. A tool that fails returns isError: true with the error text, for example "Sample Item nope not found". Protocol errors (bad JSON, unknown method) return a JSON-RPC error.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tool Arguments Annotation Description search_doctypes query, limit read-only Find DocType names that contain the query. get_doctype_schema doctype read-only Fields and permissions of a DocType. search_methods query read-only Search whitelisted methods and document methods. get_method_schema method, doctype read-only Arguments and docstring of a method. list_document_methods doctype read-only Whitelisted document methods of a DocType. list_documents doctype, filters, fields, order_by, start, limit read-only Like frappe.get_list. get_document doctype, name read-only One document with child tables. count_documents doctype, filters read-only Count matching documents. create_document doctype, data not destructive Insert a document. update_document doctype, name, data destructive Change fields of a document. delete_document doctype, name destructive Delete a document. call_method method, args destructive Call a whitelisted method or an API Server Script. call_document_method doctype, name, method, args destructive Call a whitelisted controller method, such as submit.

Tool arguments take the same values as the matching REST API v2 endpoints. Arguments are validated strictly: unknown arguments and wrong types fail. get_document, create_document and update_document always return the full document. Tool results are text and structured JSON only. A method that returns a file gives no file content to the model.

docs.title: API discovery endpoints
docs.text:
All endpoints use GET and need the Desk User role.

Route Returns /api/v2/discovery Counts of methods and document methods, and the links below. /api/v2/discovery/search?q=<words> Up to 50 methods whose path or docstring has all the words. /api/v2/discovery/method Index of all whitelisted methods. /api/v2/discovery/method/<dotted.path> One method: HTTP methods, allow_guest, parameters with types and defaults, endpoint, docstring and source. /api/v2/discovery/doctype/<doctype> Whitelisted controller methods of a DocType. /api/v2/discovery/doctype/<doctype>/method/<method> One controller method: endpoint, HTTP methods, required permission per HTTP method, parameters, docstring. 
curl "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/v2/discovery/method/frappe.client.get_value" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>"

{"data": {"type": "method", "kind": "rpc", "path": "frappe.client.get_value", "name": "get_value",
  "http_methods": ["GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE"], "allow_guest": false,
  "params": [{"name": "doctype", "required": true, "type": "str"},
             {"name": "fieldname", "required": true, "type": "str | list[str] | dict[str, Any]"}, "..."],
  "endpoint": "/api/v2/method/frappe.client.get_value",
  "docstring": "Return a value from a document. ...",
  "source": "@frappe.whitelist()\ndef get_value(..."}}

docs.title: The discovery cache
docs.text:
Frappe builds the method index in a background job on the long queue, with the job ID api-v2-discovery-build. It keeps the index in Redis for 1 hour. The job starts when an endpoint finds the cache empty. That request returns HTTP 503 with "API discovery cache is being generated. Please try again in 10 seconds." Retry after the job ends.

The index is built by reading the Python files of each app for functions with @frappe.whitelist. API Server Scripts are listed for users who can read them.

docs.title: Make your methods easy to discover
docs.text:
• Add type hints to every argument. Discovery shows them as type.
  • Write a docstring. The first line is the description in search results. The search also reads the docstring.
  • Source code is returned only when the app sets expose_discovery_source = True in hooks.py. Frappe sets it. Leave it out of a closed-source app.
# sample_app/hooks.py
expose_discovery_source = True

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_open_orders(customer: str, limit: int = 20) -> list[dict]:
    """Return open Sample Orders of a customer, newest first."""
    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Order",
        filters={"customer_name": customer, "status": "Open"},
        fields=["name", "order_date", "total"],
        order_by="order_date desc",
        limit=limit,
    )

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• An agent can do everything its user can do. Give agents their own user with only the roles they need.
  • call_method reaches every whitelisted method the user may call. Check permissions in your methods. See Whitelisted Methods.
  • A new method does not show in discovery until the cache is rebuilt. Wait up to 1 hour for the cache to expire, or run bench --site <site> clear-cache.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text:
Every Frappe site has a REST API at /api. It gives access to every DocType and every whitelisted method, with the permissions of the authenticated user. There are two versions:

  • /api/v1/... (also served at /api/...). Routes resource and method. Results are in data or message.
  • /api/v2/.... Routes document, doctype and method. Results are in data. Errors are a list in errors.

Use v2 for new clients. All requests on this page were sent with curl to http://frappe.localhost:8006 as user1@example.com. The responses are trimmed. To get a token, see Authentication.

S=http://frappe.localhost:8006
AUTH="Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>"

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
Action v1 v2 List documents GET /api/resource/<doctype> GET /api/v2/document/<doctype> Create POST /api/resource/<doctype> POST /api/v2/document/<doctype> Read GET /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> GET /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> Update PUT /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> PUT or PATCH /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> Delete DELETE /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> DELETE /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> Call a document method POST /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> with run_method, or GET with ?run_method=<method> GET or POST /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/method/<method> Call a method on an unsaved document /api/method/run_doc_method with method and docs /api/v2/method/run_doc_method with method and document Copy a document GET /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/copy Count GET /api/v2/doctype/<doctype>/count DocType metadata GET /api/v2/doctype/<doctype>/meta Call a whitelisted method /api/method/<dotted.path> /api/v2/method/<dotted.path> Call a function in a DocType module /api/v2/method/<doctype>/<function>

URL-encode spaces in DocType names (Sample%20Item). Trailing slashes are optional. The v2 routes for discovery and MCP are described in MCP and discovery. The full list is in REST endpoints.

docs.title: v1
docs.text:
curl -s -G "$S/api/resource/Sample%20Item" -H "$AUTH" \
  --data-urlencode 'fields=["name","rate"]' \
  --data-urlencode 'filters=[["category","=","Hardware"],["rate","<",100]]' \
  --data-urlencode 'order_by=rate asc'

{"data": [{"name": "Keyboard", "rate": 45.0}]}

GET /api/resource/<doctype> calls frappe.client.get_list with the query parameters:

Parameter Default Description fields ["name"] JSON list. Same syntax as frappe.get_list. filters none JSON dict or list. See Filters. or_filters none JSON dict or list, joined with OR. order_by DocType sort settings For example rate desc. group_by none Field name. limit_start 0 Offset. limit_page_length or limit 20 Page size. 0 returns all rows. as_dict 1 0 returns lists instead of objects. parent none Parent DocType, required for a child DocType. expand none JSON list of Link fields to replace with the linked document. debug 0 Print the query for debugging. 
curl -s -G "$S/api/resource/Sample%20Item" -H "$AUTH" \
  --data-urlencode 'fields=["name","rate"]' --data-urlencode 'as_dict=0' --data-urlencode 'limit=2'

{"data": [["Antivirus", 60.0], ["Installation", 80.0]]}

docs.title: v2
docs.text:
curl -s -G "$S/api/v2/document/Sample%20Item" -H "$AUTH" \
  --data-urlencode 'fields=["name","rate"]' \
  --data-urlencode 'filters={"category":"Hardware"}' \
  --data-urlencode 'order_by=rate desc' \
  --data-urlencode 'limit=2'

{"has_next_page": true, "data": [{"name": "Laptop", "rate": 900.0}, {"name": "Monitor", "rate": 250.0}]}

Next page, with start=2:

{"has_next_page": false, "data": [{"name": "Keyboard", "rate": 45.0}]}
Parameter Default Description fields ["name"] JSON list. filters none JSON dict or list. order_by DocType sort settings String. group_by none String. start 0 Offset. limit 20 Page size. limit=0 returns no rows, with has_next_page set to true. as_dict true Read, but rows are always objects. as_dict=0 also returns objects. debug false Print the query in the server log.

has_next_page tells you if another page exists. v2 builds the query with frappe.qb.get_query(..., ignore_permissions=False). A DocType controller can change it with a static method:

# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
import frappe
from frappe.model.document import Document


class SampleOrder(Document):
    @staticmethod
    def get_list(query):
        Order = frappe.qb.DocType("Sample Order")
        return query.where(Order.status != "Cancelled")

The method gets the query builder object and returns a query or None. Virtual DocTypes use their own get_list.

docs.title: Count
docs.text:
curl -s -G "$S/api/v2/doctype/Sample%20Item/count" -H "$AUTH" --data-urlencode 'filters={"category":"Hardware"}'

{"data": 3}

docs.title: Create a document
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$S/api/v2/document/Sample%20Item" -H "$AUTH" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"item_name": "Sample Mouse", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 25}'

{"data": {"name": "Sample Mouse", "owner": "user1@example.com", "creation": "2026-11-22 05:47:06.266581",
  "modified": "2026-11-22 05:47:06.266581", "modified_by": "user1@example.com", "docstatus": 0, "idx": 0,
  "item_name": "Sample Mouse", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 25.0, "disabled": 0, "description": null,
  "doctype": "Sample Item"}}

The body is the document as JSON. Include child rows as lists, for example "items": [{"item": "Laptop", "qty": 1}]. The document is inserted with doc.insert(), so validations, controller hooks and permission checks run. v1 POST /api/resource/<doctype> does the same.

docs.title: Read a document
docs.text:
curl -s "$S/api/v2/document/Sample%20Item/Sample%20Mouse" -H "$AUTH"

{"data": {"name": "Sample Mouse", "owner": "user1@example.com", "docstatus": 0, "idx": 0,
  "item_name": "Sample Mouse", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 25.0, "disabled": 0, "description": null,
  "doctype": "Sample Item"}}

The response has all fields and child tables. v2 does not read a fields parameter on this route. Both versions load the document with frappe.get_doc, check read permission, and remove fields that the user cannot read (doc.apply_fieldlevel_read_permissions). v1 accepts expand_links=1 to replace Link values with the linked documents.

docs.title: Update a document
docs.text:
curl -s -X PATCH "$S/api/v2/document/Sample%20Item/Sample%20Mouse" -H "$AUTH" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"rate": 30}'

{"data": {"name": "Sample Mouse", "modified": "2026-11-22 05:47:06.303091", "rate": 30.0, "doctype": "Sample Item"}}

The response has the full document. It is trimmed here. Send only the fields to change. Frappe loads the document with for_update=True, checks write, applies the values and calls doc.save(). A list for a table field replaces all child rows. v1 uses PUT /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> with the same body.

docs.title: Delete a document
docs.text:
curl -s -X DELETE "$S/api/v2/document/Sample%20Item/Sample%20Mouse" -H "$AUTH" -w '\n%{http_code}\n'

{"data":"ok"}
202

docs.title: Call methods
docs.text:
curl -s "$S/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" -H "$AUTH"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}
curl -s "$S/api/v2/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" -H "$AUTH"
# {"data":"user1@example.com"}
curl -s "$S/api/v2/method/User/get_current_user_roles" -H "$AUTH"
# {"data":["Sample Role","All","Guest","Desk User"]}

Send arguments as query parameters for GET, and as a JSON or form body for POST. Nested values (lists, dicts) need a JSON body or JSON-encoded parameters. See Whitelisted methods.

frappe.client has general methods, for example frappe.client.get_list, frappe.client.get_value, frappe.client.insert, frappe.client.set_value, frappe.client.submit, frappe.client.cancel and frappe.client.delete. They apply the permissions of the user.

curl -s -X POST "$S/api/v2/method/frappe.client.insert" -H "$AUTH" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"doc": {"doctype": "Sample Item", "item_name": "Sample Mouse C", "category": "Hardware"}}'

docs.title: Responses
docs.text: Key Where Content data v1 resource, all v2 Result message v1 method Return value of the method has_next_page v2 list true if more rows exist docs v2 document methods The document after the method ran _server_messages v1 JSON string with messages from frappe.msgprint messages v2 List of messages from frappe.msgprint

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The HTTP status comes from http_status_code of the exception class (frappe/exceptions.py):

Status Exception 400 frappe.CSRFTokenError 401 frappe.AuthenticationError 403 frappe.PermissionError 404 frappe.DoesNotExistError 409 frappe.DuplicateEntryError (subclass of frappe.NameError) 417 frappe.ValidationError and subclasses (for example frappe.MandatoryError, frappe.TimestampMismatchError), frappe.FrappeTypeError 429 frappe.RateLimitExceededError, frappe.TooManyRequestsError 500 Other exceptions

v1 error:

{"exception": "frappe.exceptions.PermissionError: Insufficient Permission for <strong>Sample Order</strong>",
 "exc_type": "PermissionError",
 "_server_messages": "[\"{\\\"message\\\":\\\"Insufficient Permission for <strong>Sample Order</strong>\\\", ...}\"]"}

v2 error:

{"errors": [{"type": "PermissionError",
  "message": "Insufficient Permission for <strong>Sample Order</strong>",
  "as_table": false, "title": "Permission Error", "indicator": "red"}]}

The traceback (exc in v1, exception in v2) is sent when the DEV_SERVER environment variable is set, or when System Settings allow_error_traceback is on and the user is a system user. A 404 response has no traceback.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text: A POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE request commits on success. A GET request is rolled back, unless the code sets frappe.local.flags.commit. Any error rolls back the request. See Transactions.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• The list default is 20 rows. Pass limit=0 (v1) or a larger limit (v2) to get more. In v2, limit=0 returns no rows.
  • JSON parameters in a GET URL must be URL-encoded. Use curl -G --data-urlencode.
  • v1 sends results in data for resources and in message for methods. v2 always uses data.
  • has_next_page only exists in v2.

docs.title: Whitelisted Methods
docs.text: A whitelisted method is a Python function that clients can call over HTTP. Add @frappe.whitelist() to a function in your app, and it becomes available at /api/method/<dotted.path> and /api/v2/method/<dotted.path>. The desk calls these methods with frappe.call. Functions without the decorator cannot be called from a client.

docs.title: Write a method
docs.text:
# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_items(category: str, limit: int = 20) -> list[dict]:
    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Item",
        filters={"category": category, "disabled": 0},
        fields=["name", "rate"],
        order_by="rate desc",
        limit=limit,
    )

Call it:

curl -G "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/sample_app.api.get_items" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>" \
  --data-urlencode "category=Hardware" --data-urlencode "limit=2"

{"message": [{"name": "Laptop", "rate": 900.0}, {"name": "Monitor", "rate": 250.0}]}

How the call works (frappe/handler.py):

  1. The path after /api/method/ is the dotted path of the function.
  2. Frappe applies override_whitelisted_methods hooks.
  3. If a Server Script of type API has the same method name, the script runs instead.
  4. Frappe imports the function and checks that it is whitelisted and that the HTTP method is allowed.
  5. Frappe calls the function with the request parameters (frappe.form_dict). Parameters that the function does not declare are dropped, unless it has **kwargs.
  6. The return value goes into message (v1) or data (v2) of the JSON response.

The parameters ignore_permissions and flags are always removed before the call (frappe.get_newargs).

docs.title: Decorator options
docs.text:
frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=False, xss_safe=False, methods=None)
Name Type Default Description allow_guest bool False Allow calls from users who are not logged in. xss_safe bool False With allow_guest: do not sanitize HTML in string arguments of guest calls. methods list all Allowed HTTP methods. Default: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE.

docs.title: methods
docs.text:
A call with another HTTP method raises frappe.PermissionError (HTTP 403):

curl "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.client.set_value?doctype=Sample%20Item&name=Laptop&fieldname=rate&value=1" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>"

{"exception": "frappe.exceptions.PermissionError: Not permitted", "exc_type": "PermissionError"}

frappe.client.set_value declares methods=["POST", "PUT"].

Warning

Frappe rolls back the transaction at the end of every GET request. A method that writes data must declare methods=["POST"] (or PUT, DELETE). See Transactions.

docs.title: allow_guest
docs.text:
# sample_app/api.py
import frappe
from frappe.rate_limiter import rate_limit


@frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True, methods=["POST"])
@rate_limit(limit=5, seconds=60 * 60)
def subscribe(email: str):
    frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "Sample Subscriber", "email": email}).insert(ignore_permissions=True)

For guest calls, Frappe sanitizes HTML in every string argument of frappe.form_dict with frappe.utils.sanitize_html, unless xss_safe=True.

Declare methods and add a @rate_limit(...) below @frappe.whitelist on every guest method.

docs.title: Type annotations
docs.text:
The decorator wraps the function with validate_argument_types (frappe/utils/typing_validations.py). During a request (and in tests), Frappe validates each annotated argument with pydantic:

  • Values are converted when the conversion is safe. The string "2" becomes 2 for an int argument.
  • A value that does not match raises frappe.FrappeTypeError (HTTP 417).
  • The type of the default value is also accepted. limit: int = None accepts None.
  • String annotations and forward references are not validated. This includes all annotations in a module with from __future__ import annotations.
  • Direct Python calls outside a request are not validated.
curl -G "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.desk.search.get_names_for_mentions" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>" \
  --data-urlencode "search_term=user" --data-urlencode "page_length=two"

{"exception": "frappe.exceptions.FrappeTypeError: Argument 'page_length' in 'frappe.desk.search.get_names_for_mentions' should be of type 'int' but got 'str' instead.", "exc_type": "FrappeTypeError"}

Arguments without an annotation are not validated.

Version

frappe/hooks.py sets require_type_annotated_api_methods = True, but no code in v16 reads this hook. Whitelisted methods without annotations still work.

docs.title: Check access
docs.text:
The decorator only decides who can call the function. It does not check data permissions. Check them in the function:

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def close_order(name: str):
    doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name)
    doc.check_permission("write")
    doc.status = "Completed"
    doc.save()
    return doc.status
Tool Use it to frappe.only_for(roles, message=False) Allow only users with one of the roles. Raises frappe.PermissionError. frappe.has_permission(doctype, ptype, doc, throw=True) Check a right on a DocType or document. doc.check_permission(ptype) Check a right on a loaded document. frappe.get_list(...) Query with the permissions of the user.

frappe.core.doctype.user.user.generate_keys is an example. It starts with frappe.only_for("System Manager"). A call from another user returns HTTP 403. See Permissions.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
frappe.rate_limiter.rate_limit limits calls per endpoint. It counts calls in Redis.

rate_limit(key=None, limit=5, seconds=86400, methods="ALL", ip_based=True, endpoint=None, user_based=False)
Name Type Default Description key str None Name of a request parameter. Its value is added to the counter key, for example "email". limit int or callable 5 Maximum calls in the window. A callable is evaluated on each call. seconds int 86400 Window length. methods str or list "ALL" Limit only these HTTP methods. ip_based bool True Count per client IP. user_based bool False Count per logged-in user. Guests are counted per IP. endpoint str None Counter name. Required when the function has no stable dotted path, for example a functools.partial.

When the limit is reached, the call raises frappe.RateLimitExceededError (HTTP 429). The limit applies only to HTTP requests. Direct Python calls are not counted.

Warning

Put @rate_limit below @frappe.whitelist. If it is above, the registered function is not the one that the module exports, and the method is not whitelisted.

The site config key rate_limit ({"limit": <seconds>, "window": <seconds>}) is a separate limit. It limits the total request processing time per site in each window. Over the limit, requests get HTTP 429, and responses carry X-RateLimit-* headers. See Configuration.

docs.title: Controller methods
docs.text:
Whitelist a method of a DocType controller to call it on one document:

# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
import frappe
from frappe.model.document import Document


class SampleOrder(Document):
    @frappe.whitelist()
    def mark_completed(self):
        self.status = "Completed"
        self.save()
Route Permission checked POST /api/resource/Sample Order/SO-00001 with run_method=mark_completed write GET /api/resource/Sample Order/SO-00001?run_method=mark_completed read POST /api/v2/document/Sample Order/SO-00001/method/mark_completed write GET /api/v2/document/Sample Order/SO-00001/method/mark_completed read

The method also needs @frappe.whitelist(), and the HTTP method must be in its methods. In the desk, call it with frm.call("mark_completed"). See Form scripts.

A module-level function in a DocType module can be called by DocType name in v2: /api/v2/method/<DocType>/<function>. For example /api/v2/method/User/get_current_user_roles calls frappe.core.doctype.user.user.get_current_user_roles.

docs.title: Override a method of another app
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
override_whitelisted_methods = {
    "frappe.desk.doctype.event.event.get_events": "sample_app.overrides.get_events",
}
  • The key is the dotted path that clients call. The value is your function.
  • The new function must also be whitelisted.
  • If several apps override the same path, the app installed last wins.
  • The override applies to HTTP calls only. Python code that imports the original function still calls it.

See Extending apps.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A whitelisted method is a public endpoint. Validate every argument and check permissions in the function.
  • Do not use frappe.get_all or ignore_permissions=True to return data to the caller unless all callers may see all rows.
  • Do not build SQL from arguments. Use the Query builder or parameters.
  • Return values must be JSON serializable.

docs.title: Building Apps
docs.text:
Create an app, use hooks, extend other apps, ship fixtures and patches, and translate.

Page What it covers Apps Create a Frappe app, understand its files and folders, install it on a site, and build its assets. Hooks How hooks.py works, how hook values from all apps merge, and the hooks that apps use most. Extending Other Apps Change the behavior of DocTypes and methods from another app with doc_events, controller overrides and mixins, method overrides, doctype_js, custom fields and property setters. Fixtures and Patches Ship records with an app through the fixtures hook, change data on existing sites with patches, and understand the order of bench migrate. Translations Mark strings with _() in Python and __() in JS, use context and lazy strings, keep PO/POT files in an app, and run the bench translation commands.

docs.title: Apps
docs.text: An app is a Python package that adds DocTypes, pages, hooks, APIs and assets to a site. All your code goes in an app. Do not edit frappe or other apps that you do not own. Use an app when you need code-level changes. Use Customize Form or Server and Client Scripts for small changes that a site admin can make.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
• A bench holds many apps in apps/. The file sites/apps.txt lists the apps on the bench.
  • A site uses only the apps that are installed on it. The list is stored in the installed_apps global default.
  • An app has one or more modules. Each module is a folder in the app package. DocTypes, reports and pages belong to a module.
  • frappe is always the first app. Other apps follow in the order of installation.

See Architecture for the bench, site and app model.

docs.title: Create an app
docs.text:
1. Go to the bench root.
  2. Run bench new-app.
cd ~/frappe-bench
bench new-app sample_app

bench new-app is a command of the bench CLI. It calls the Frappe command bench make-app apps sample_app. Then it installs the package into the bench virtual environment, adds the app to sites/apps.txt and builds assets.

bench make-app DESTINATION APP_NAME writes only the files. Use --no-git to skip git init. The app name is converted to snake case with frappe.scrub. The command stops if a site has the same name as the app.

The command asks these questions:

Prompt Default Notes App Title App name in title case Must start with a letter. Letters, numbers, spaces and underscores only. App Description none App Publisher none App Email none Must be a valid email address. App License mit Choices come from the GitHub licenses API. Create GitHub Workflow action for unittests False Adds .github/workflows/ci.yml and linter.yml. Branch Name Current branch of frappe Used for git init and the CI workflow.

docs.title: Files and folders
docs.text:
bench make-app makes this tree (frappe/utils/boilerplate.py):

apps/sample_app/                  # git repository
├── pyproject.toml
├── README.md
├── license.txt
├── .gitignore                    # not written with --no-git
├── .pre-commit-config.yaml
├── .editorconfig
├── .eslintrc
├── .github/workflows/            # only if you answer yes to the workflow prompt
└── sample_app/                   # Python package
    ├── __init__.py               # __version__ = "0.0.1"
    ├── hooks.py
    ├── modules.txt
    ├── patches.txt
    ├── config/__init__.py
    ├── patches/__init__.py
    ├── public/
    │   ├── .gitkeep
    │   ├── css/
    │   └── js/
    ├── templates/
    │   ├── __init__.py
    │   ├── includes/
    │   └── pages/__init__.py
    ├── www/
    └── sample_app/               # first module, named from the App Title
        ├── __init__.py
        └── .frappe
Path Purpose pyproject.toml Package metadata. Build backend is flit_core. The version is read from __init__.py. sample_app/__init__.py Holds __version__. sample_app/hooks.py App metadata and hooks. See Hooks. sample_app/modules.txt One module name per line. frappe.get_module_list reads the modules of an app from this file. sample_app/patches.txt Patches that bench migrate runs. It has the sections [pre_model_sync] and [post_model_sync]. See Fixtures and Patches. sample_app/public/ Static assets. Served at /assets/sample_app/. sample_app/templates/ Jinja templates for web pages and includes. sample_app/www/ Web pages that map to URL paths. See Website. sample_app/<module>/ A module folder. The boilerplate also writes an empty .frappe file in it.

The first module folder name is the scrubbed App Title. For the title "Sample App" it is sample_app. This is the same as the package name, so the path is sample_app/sample_app/sample_app/.

docs.title: pyproject.toml
docs.text:
The generated file sets requires-python = ">=3.14" and ruff settings. Two bench-specific tables are present:

Table Use [tool.bench.dev-dependencies] Python packages that bench installs only when developer mode is on. [deploy.dependencies.apt] packages list of apt packages for Frappe Cloud.

Do not add frappe to dependencies. Bench installs and manages it.

docs.title: Module folders
docs.text:
When you save a standard DocType in developer mode, Frappe writes its files into the module folder:

sample_app/selling/                 # module "Selling"
└── doctype/
    └── sample_order/
        ├── __init__.py
        ├── sample_order.json       # the DocType definition
        ├── sample_order.py         # the controller
        ├── sample_order.js         # the form script
        └── test_sample_order.py    # the test file

Folder and file names are the scrubbed names (lowercase, spaces become underscores). See DocTypes for the JSON and Controllers for the Python class.

To add a module, add its name to modules.txt, make the folder with an __init__.py, and run bench --site <site> migrate. bench migrate adds missing Module Def records for every installed app.

docs.title: Install an app on a site
docs.text:
1. Get the app into the bench. Use bench new-app or bench get-app <git-url>.
  2. Install it on the site.
bench --site frappe.localhost install-app sample_app

install-app accepts more than one app. Use --force to install again over an existing install.

frappe.installer.install_app runs these steps in this order:

  1. Install each app in required_apps first.
  2. If the app is already installed, print a message and stop. --force skips this check.
  3. Print a warning if the app overrides a DocType class that another app already overrides.
  4. Check that the user has the System Manager role (not for frappe).
  5. Run the before_install hooks of the app. If one returns False, stop.
  6. Run the before_app_install hooks of the installed apps. Each gets the app name.
  7. Add a Module Def for each module in modules.txt.
  8. Sync all DocTypes of the app from their JSON files.
  9. Add the app to installed_apps and commit.
  10. Run the after_install hooks of the app.
  11. Mark all patches in patches.txt as done. A new install does not run old patches.
  12. Run the after_app_install hooks of the installed apps.
  13. Sync scheduled jobs, fixtures, customizations and dashboards.
  14. Run the after_sync hooks of the app.

If a step after step 9 fails, Frappe rolls back and removes the app from installed_apps.

To remove an app from a site, use bench --site <site> uninstall-app sample_app. Add --dry-run to list the DocTypes that it deletes. Other options are --yes (no prompt), --no-backup and --force.

docs.title: Required apps
docs.text:
Declare other apps that your app needs in hooks.py:

# sample_app/hooks.py
required_apps = ["frappe/erpnext"]

An entry can be an app name (erpnext), an org/repo (frappe/erpnext) or a git URL. install-app installs the required apps first. bench get-app --resolve-deps also fetches them.

docs.title: Build assets
docs.text:
Frappe bundles files whose name matches *.bundle.{js,ts,css,sass,scss,less,styl,jsx} under public/. Other files in public/ are served as they are.

bench build --app sample_app
Option Description --app TEXT Build assets for one app. --apps TEXT Build assets for some apps. --production Build in production mode. --hard-link Copy the files instead of making symlinks. --force Build the assets instead of downloading available ones. --save-metafiles Save esbuild metafiles to analyze bundle size. --using-cached Use cached build artifacts. Ignored in developer mode. --verbose Show more output.

sites/assets/sample_app is a symlink to apps/sample_app/sample_app/public. Built bundles go into public/dist/. Include a bundle in the desk with the app_include_js or app_include_css hook:

# sample_app/hooks.py
app_include_js = "sample_app.bundle.js"     # built from public/js/sample_app.bundle.js
app_include_css = "sample_app.bundle.css"

During development, bench watch rebuilds bundles when files change. The watch process in the bench Procfile runs it. Use bench watch --apps sample_app to watch some apps only.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not delete public/.gitkeep. Without the public folder, bench build does not link the assets of the app.
  • bench make-app does not install the app into the environment. Use bench new-app, or run bench get-app on the folder.
  • A new module is not visible on a site until modules.txt lists it and you run bench migrate.
  • You can save standard DocTypes only in developer mode. Set developer_mode to 1 in site_config.json on your development site. See Configuration.

docs.title: Extending Other Apps
docs.text: Use the hooks on this page when your app must change a DocType or a method that another app owns. Do not edit the other app. Your changes stay in your app and survive updates of the other app. Each hook goes in your app's hooks.py. Frappe merges the hook values of all installed apps. For how merging works, see Hooks.

docs.title: Choose a mechanism
docs.text: Need Use Run code when a document of another app is saved, submitted, deleted doc_events Add methods or change methods of another app's controller extend_doctype_class (mixin) Replace the controller class of a DocType override_doctype_class Replace a whitelisted method override_whitelisted_methods Add form, list, tree or calendar JavaScript to another app's DocType doctype_js, doctype_list_js, doctype_tree_js, doctype_calendar_js, doctype_kanban_js Add fields to another app's DocType Custom Field (create_custom_fields or exported customizations) Change a property of a field or DocType (label, hidden, reqd, options) Property Setter (make_property_setter) Replace the link search query of a DocType standard_queries Change the dashboard (connections) of a DocType override_doctype_dashboards Send extra data to the desk on page load boot_session

docs.title: doc_events
docs.text:
doc_events maps a DocType name (or "*" for all DocTypes) to controller events. Each event has a dotted path or a list of dotted paths.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doc_events = {
    "ToDo": {
        "validate": "sample_app.events.todo.validate",
        "on_update": ["sample_app.events.todo.notify_owner"],
    },
    "*": {
        "on_trash": "sample_app.events.common.log_delete",
    },
}

# sample_app/events/todo.py
import frappe
from frappe import _


def validate(doc, method=None):
    if doc.priority == "High" and not doc.date:
        frappe.throw(_("Set a due date for high priority tasks"))
  • The handler gets the document and the event name. A handler that has no method parameter is also accepted: def validate(doc).
  • Handlers run after the controller method of the same name (Document.hook in frappe/model/document.py). Handlers of the DocType run before the handlers of "*".
  • frappe.db.commit() and frappe.db.rollback() inside a handler do not run. Frappe shows a warning and returns. Use frappe.db.after_commit.add(fn) for side effects that must happen after the commit.
  • Any event that run_method calls works: before_insert, validate, on_update, on_submit, on_cancel, on_trash, after_insert and others. See Controllers for the order.

docs.title: extend_doctype_class
docs.text:
extend_doctype_class adds mixin classes to the controller of a DocType. Frappe builds a new class with the mixins first and the original controller last. This lets several apps extend one DocType without conflict.

# sample_app/hooks.py
extend_doctype_class = {
    "ToDo": "sample_app.overrides.todo.ToDoMixin",
}

# sample_app/overrides/todo.py
import frappe


class ToDoMixin:
    def validate(self):
        super().validate()
        self.description = (self.description or "").strip()

    @frappe.whitelist()
    def mark_urgent(self):
        self.priority = "High"
        self.save()
  • Call super() in a method that also exists on the controller. Otherwise the original method does not run.
  • When more than one app extends a DocType, the mixin of the app listed last in the hook list comes first in the MRO.
  • The extended class gets the name Extended<ClassName>. Code that checks type(doc).__name__ sees this name.

docs.title: override_doctype_class
docs.text:
override_doctype_class replaces the controller class. Only the last value is used, so only one app can override a DocType.

# sample_app/hooks.py
override_doctype_class = {
    "ToDo": "sample_app.overrides.todo.CustomToDo",
}

# sample_app/overrides/todo.py
from frappe.desk.doctype.todo.todo import ToDo


class CustomToDo(ToDo):
    def on_update(self):
        super().on_update()
        # your code
  • The class must be a subclass of the original controller. If it is not, get_controller raises "must be a subclass of" with the title "Invalid Override".
  • bench install-app and bench migrate print a warning when more than one app overrides the same DocType.
  • extend_doctype_class mixins are applied on top of the override. Prefer extend_doctype_class when you only add or change a few methods.

docs.title: override_whitelisted_methods
docs.text:
override_whitelisted_methods maps the dotted path of a whitelisted method to your replacement. The last app in the hook list wins.

# sample_app/hooks.py
override_whitelisted_methods = {
    "frappe.desk.doctype.event.event.get_events": "sample_app.overrides.event.get_events",
}
  • The override applies to /api/method/<path> and /api/v2/method/<path> (frappe/handler.py, frappe/api/v2.py).
  • The replacement must also have @frappe.whitelist(). Frappe checks the replacement, not the original.
  • Keep the same parameters as the original. Callers do not know about the override.
  • The hook does not change Python calls to the original function. It changes only HTTP calls.

docs.title: doctype_js and related hooks
docs.text:
These hooks add JavaScript files from your app to the views of another app's DocType. The path is relative to your app package.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doctype_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo.js"}
doctype_list_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo_list.js"}

// sample_app/public/js/todo.js
frappe.ui.form.on("ToDo", {
    refresh(frm) {
        frm.add_custom_button(__("Mark Urgent"), () => {
            frm.call("mark_urgent").then(() => frm.reload_doc());
        });
    },
});

Frappe reads the file on each meta load and appends it to the form script (frappe/desk/form/meta.py). You do not need to build assets for these files. The value can be a list of paths. See Form Scripts for the form API.

docs.title: Custom fields from code
docs.text:
Use create_custom_fields to add fields to another app's DocType. Call it from after_install and from after_migrate, so that the fields also exist on sites that update.

# sample_app/hooks.py
after_install = "sample_app.setup.make_custom_fields"
after_migrate = "sample_app.setup.make_custom_fields"

# sample_app/setup.py
from frappe.custom.doctype.custom_field.custom_field import create_custom_fields


def make_custom_fields():
    create_custom_fields(
        {
            "ToDo": [
                {
                    "fieldname": "sample_code",
                    "label": "Sample Code",
                    "fieldtype": "Data",
                    "insert_after": "description",
                },
            ],
        }
    )

create_custom_fields(custom_fields, ignore_validate=False, update=True):

Name Type Default Description custom_fields dict Key: a DocType name or a tuple of names. Value: one field dict or a list of field dicts. ignore_validate bool False Skip field validation. update bool True Update fields that exist. If False, only missing fields are inserted.
  • Fields are created with owner Administrator and is_system_generated set. Only Administrator can delete them from the desk.
  • The function clears the DocType cache and adds the columns with frappe.db.updatedb.
  • delete_custom_fields({"ToDo": ["sample_code"]}) removes fields. It does not drop the database column.

docs.title: Exported customizations
docs.text: In developer mode, Customize Form has an Export Customizations action. It writes Custom Fields and Property Setters of a DocType to <app>/<module>/custom/<doctype>.json (export_customizations in frappe/modules/utils.py). If the file has "sync_on_migrate": 1, bench migrate syncs it on every site. Use this when you build the fields in the desk. Use create_custom_fields when you prefer to keep fields in Python.

docs.title: Property setters from code
docs.text:
A Property Setter changes one property of a DocType or of a field, without changing the DocType JSON.

from frappe.custom.doctype.property_setter.property_setter import make_property_setter

make_property_setter("ToDo", "priority", "default", "High", "Data")
make_property_setter("ToDo", None, "sort_field", "date", "Data", for_doctype=True)

make_property_setter(doctype, fieldname, property, value, property_type, for_doctype=False, validate_fields_for_doctype=True, is_system_generated=True):

  • Ignores permissions.
  • Deletes the old Property Setter for the same DocType, field and property, then inserts the new one. The name is <doctype>-<field or "main">-<property>.
  • Clears the DocType cache.

frappe.make_property_setter(args, ...) is a second form. It takes a dict with doctype, fieldname, property, value and optional property_type. If doctype is not set, it applies to every DocType that has a field with that fieldname.

docs.title: standard_queries
docs.text:
standard_queries replaces the search query that Link fields use for a DocType. Frappe uses the last value. The method must be whitelisted.

# sample_app/hooks.py
standard_queries = {"Sample Item": "sample_app.queries.sample_item_query"}

# sample_app/queries.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
@frappe.validate_and_sanitize_search_inputs
def sample_item_query(doctype, txt, searchfield, start, page_len, filters):
    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Item",
        filters={"disabled": 0, "item_name": ["like", f"%{txt}%"]},
        fields=["name", "item_name"],
        limit_start=start,
        limit_page_length=page_len,
        as_list=True,
    )

Frappe calls the method with doctype, txt, searchfield, start, page_len, filters (frappe/desk/search.py). A query set by a form script with frm.set_query takes priority over this hook.

docs.title: override_doctype_dashboards
docs.text:
Each method gets the dashboard data as data and returns the changed data. Frappe calls all methods in order (frappe/model/meta.py).

# sample_app/hooks.py
override_doctype_dashboards = {"ToDo": "sample_app.overrides.todo.get_dashboard_data"}

# sample_app/overrides/todo.py
def get_dashboard_data(data):
    data.setdefault("transactions", []).append({"label": "Sample", "items": ["Sample Order"]})
    return data

The data dict can be empty when the DocType has no <doctype>_dashboard.py file. Use setdefault for keys that can be missing.

docs.title: boot_session
docs.text:
Each method gets the bootinfo dict before the desk loads (frappe/boot.py). Add keys to it. The client reads them from frappe.boot.

# sample_app/hooks.py
boot_session = "sample_app.boot.boot_session"

# sample_app/boot.py
def boot_session(bootinfo):
    bootinfo.sample_app_settings = {"show_banner": True}

The method runs on every desk load. Keep it fast. Do not run queries per DocType or per record.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• override_doctype_class allows one winner. Two apps that override the same DocType break each other. Use extend_doctype_class instead.
  • A doc_events handler runs for every save, also for imports and API calls. Check doc.flags or field changes with doc.has_value_changed("field") before you do heavy work.
  • Do not call frappe.db.commit() in a doc_events handler. It does not run, and the transaction stays open.
  • create_custom_fields only runs where you call it. Call it from after_migrate too, or sites that update do not get new fields.
  • doctype_js files are not bundled. Do not use import statements in them.

docs.title: Fixtures and Patches
docs.text: Fixtures and patches move data with your app. Use fixtures for records that must be the same on every site, such as Custom Fields, Property Setters, Roles or Workflows. Use patches for one-time changes to the data of sites that already exist, such as a field rename or a backfill. Both run during bench migrate.

docs.title: Declare fixtures
docs.text:
Add the fixtures hook to hooks.py. Each item is a DocType name or a dict with filters.

# sample_app/hooks.py
fixtures = [
    "Sample Role",
    {"dt": "Custom Field", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]},
    {"dt": "Property Setter", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]},
    {"doctype": "Workflow", "or_filters": [["name", "=", "Sample Order Approval"]], "prefix": "approval"},
]
Key Type Description dt or doctype str The DocType to export. filters list or dict Filters for frappe.get_all. Exports only matching records. or_filters list or dict OR filters for frappe.get_all. prefix str Adds <prefix>_ to the file name. Use it to export one DocType into more than one file.

Without filters, every record of the DocType is exported. Filter Custom Fields and Property Setters by module, or you export the customizations of all apps.

DocType and Page cannot be fixtures. export-fixtures stops with an error for these. Create them in developer mode, and Frappe writes them to the app as files.

docs.title: Export fixtures
docs.text:
Run this on a site that has the records:

bench --site frappe.localhost export-fixtures --app sample_app

Frappe writes one JSON file per fixture to sample_app/fixtures/<scrubbed_doctype>.json (for example custom_field.json). It removes owner, creation, modified_by, idx, lft and rgt from each record. Without --app, Frappe exports the fixtures of all installed apps.

To control the import order, set fixture_auto_order = True in hooks.py. Frappe then adds a number to each file name, in the order of the fixtures list, for example 1_sample_role.json.

docs.title: Import fixtures
docs.text:
bench migrate and bench install-app call sync_fixtures. It imports every .json file in <app>/fixtures/, sorted by file name.

  • An existing record with the same name is deleted and inserted again. Changes made on the site to a fixture record are lost on the next migrate.
  • A record that you remove from the JSON file is not deleted from sites.
  • If the DocType of a file does not exist, Frappe prints "Skipping fixture syncing" and goes on.
  • Emails are muted during the import. Each file is committed.
  • bench migrate --skip-fixtures skips this step.

Warning

<app>/fixtures/custom_scripts/*.js files are not imported. Frappe prints an error for each one. Export Client Scripts as a Client Script fixture instead.

docs.title: Fixtures or exported customizations
docs.text: For Custom Fields and Property Setters you can also use Export Customizations in Customize Form. That writes <app>/<module>/custom/<doctype>.json. Files with "sync_on_migrate": 1 sync on every migrate. See Extending Other Apps.

docs.title: Patches
docs.text: A patch is a Python module with an execute() function. Frappe runs each patch once per site and records it in Patch Log.

docs.title: Write a patch
docs.text:
# sample_app/patches/v1_0/set_default_category.py
import frappe


def execute():
    """Set category of old Sample Items to Hardware."""
    frappe.db.set_value(
        "Sample Item",
        {"category": ("is", "not set")},
        "category",
        "Hardware",
        update_modified=False,
    )
  • Frappe prints the docstring when the patch runs.
  • Frappe commits before and after the patch. If the patch raises an error, Frappe rolls back and stops the migrate.
  • During a patch frappe.flags.in_patch is set and developer_mode is off. Files are not written back to the app.
  • Server Script DocType events do not run during a migrate.

docs.title: Register the patch
docs.text:
Add the dotted path to <app>/patches.txt. Use the INI format with sections:

# sample_app/patches.txt
[pre_model_sync]
sample_app.patches.v1_0.rename_old_field

[post_model_sync]
sample_app.patches.v1_0.set_default_category
execute:frappe.db.set_single_value("System Settings", "enable_onboarding", 0)
Section Runs Use for [pre_model_sync] Before DocType JSON is synced Patches that need the old schema, for example to copy data out of a column that the new JSON removes. [post_model_sync] After DocType JSON is synced Most patches. New fields and DocTypes exist.
  • A file without section headers is read in the old format. All lines are pre_model_sync patches.
  • Both sections are required in INI format.
  • Patches run before fixtures and exported customizations are synced. A patch cannot use Custom Fields or records that come from fixtures of the same migrate. Use an after_migrate hook for that work.
  • A line that starts with execute: runs the Python code after the prefix.
  • A line that starts with finally: runs after all other patches of the same pass.
  • To run a patch again on all sites, change its line, for example add a comment: sample_app.patches.v1_0.set_default_category #2. Patch Log stores the full line.

docs.title: Run patches
docs.text:
bench --site frappe.localhost migrate
bench --site frappe.localhost run-patch sample_app.patches.v1_0.set_default_category
bench --site frappe.localhost run-patch --force sample_app.patches.v1_0.set_default_category

run-patch runs one patch if it is not in Patch Log. --force runs it again.

bench migrate --skip-failing writes a failing patch to Patch Log with skipped set and goes on. Frappe tries the patch again on the next migrate. To stop the migrate for a patch even with --skip-failing, list it in the never_skip_patches hook:

# sample_app/hooks.py
never_skip_patches = ["sample_app.patches.v1_0.critical_data_fix"]

docs.title: Order of bench migrate
docs.text:
SiteMigration in frappe/migrate.py runs these steps for each site. It takes a file lock, so only one migrate runs at a time.

  1. Check that Redis cache is running. If not, stop.
  2. Register new modules of installed apps.
  3. Run before_migrate hooks of each app.
  4. Run [pre_model_sync] patches.
  5. Sync DocType JSON and other standard files of all apps (frappe.model.sync.sync_all).
  6. Run [post_model_sync] patches.
  7. Sync Scheduled Job Types from scheduler_events.
  8. Sync fixtures (unless --skip-fixtures).
  9. Sync dashboards and exported customizations.
  10. Sync languages, flush deferred inserts, remove orphan DocTypes.
  11. Sync the portal menu and update Installed Applications.
  12. Run after_migrate hooks of each app.

Steps 2 to 3, 4 to 6 and 7 to 12 each commit at the end, or roll back on error. After the migrate, Frappe clears the translation and website caches. It queues a rebuild of the website search index on the long queue, unless you pass --skip-search-index. Then it sends a version-update realtime event to open desks.

# sample_app/hooks.py
before_migrate = "sample_app.migrate.before_migrate"
after_migrate = ["sample_app.setup.make_custom_fields"]

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not call frappe.get_doc and doc.save() on many records in a patch. Use frappe.db.set_value with filters, frappe.qb.update or frappe.db.bulk_update.
  • A patch in [pre_model_sync] cannot use new fields. Put patches that read old data there, and check the column with frappe.db.has_column first, because new sites never had it.
  • Fixture records are replaced on every migrate. Do not use fixtures for records that users edit.
  • A prefix in a dict fixture is also used for the next plain string fixtures in the list (frappe/utils/fixtures.py does not reset it). Put plain string fixtures before dict fixtures with a prefix, or give every fixture a dict.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: hooks.py is the file where an app tells Frappe what to add or change. Each hook is a module-level variable. Frappe reads the hooks of all installed apps and merges them. Use hooks to run code on document events, add assets, add scheduled jobs, override classes and methods, and react to install and migrate. This page explains how hooks work and shows the hooks that apps use most. For every hook key, see the Hooks reference.

docs.title: How Frappe reads hooks
docs.text:
frappe.get_hooks loads <app>.hooks for each installed app (frappe/__init__.py, _load_app_hooks):

  • Apps are read in the order of installed_apps. frappe is first.
  • Every module-level name that does not start with _ is a hook. Imported modules, functions and classes are skipped.
# sample_app/hooks.py
app_name = "sample_app"
app_title = "Sample App"

doc_events = {
    "Sample Order": {
        "on_submit": "sample_app.events.notify_customer",
    },
}

docs.title: How values merge
docs.text:
frappe.append_hook merges the value of each app into one dict:

Value in hooks.py Merged result A string or number A list. Each app appends its value. A list One list. Each app extends it. A dict A dict. Keys merge across apps, and each leaf becomes a list.

So frappe.get_hooks("app_name") returns a list, even though each app sets a string:

frappe.get_hooks("app_name")
# ['frappe']            on a site with only frappe. Each app adds its name.

frappe.get_hooks("doc_events")["*"]["on_submit"]
# ['frappe.flow.triggers.dispatch']   one list for all apps

Most hooks call every value in the list, in app order. Some hooks use only the last value:

Hook Which value wins override_whitelisted_methods The last app in installed_apps that overrides the method. override_doctype_class The last app that overrides the DocType.

docs.title: Read hooks in your code
docs.text:
# all apps
for method in frappe.get_hooks("after_migrate"):
    frappe.get_attr(method)()

# one app only
frappe.get_hooks("fixtures", app_name="sample_app")

# a default when the hook is not set
frappe.get_hooks("my_hook", default={})
Parameter Type Default Description hook str None Hook name. If None, return all hooks as a dict. default any [] Value to return when no app sets the hook. app_name str None Read the hooks of this app only.

Hooks are cached:

  • Developer mode off: in the client cache, key app_hooks.
  • Developer mode on: in process memory per site.
  • With app_name: per request.

bench --site <site> clear-cache clears the caches. Run it after you change hooks.py on a site that is not in developer mode. Also restart the bench processes, because workers keep loaded Python modules.

docs.title: App metadata
docs.text:
bench make-app writes these values. They are also read as hooks.

# sample_app/hooks.py
app_name = "sample_app"
app_title = "Sample App"
app_publisher = "Example Corp"
app_description = "Sample app"
app_email = "admin@example.com"
app_license = "mit"

The boilerplate also writes this hook as a comment:

Hook Effect export_python_type_annotations = True Saving a DocType in developer mode writes field type hints into the controller. Remove the # to turn it on. See Controllers.

Version

frappe/hooks.py in v16 sets require_type_annotated_api_methods = True, but no code reads this hook in v16. It has no effect.

docs.title: Install, uninstall and migrate
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
required_apps = ["frappe/erpnext"]

before_install = "sample_app.install.before_install"
after_install = "sample_app.install.after_install"
after_sync = "sample_app.install.after_sync"

before_uninstall = "sample_app.uninstall.before_uninstall"
after_uninstall = "sample_app.uninstall.after_uninstall"

# called with the name of the app that is installed or uninstalled
after_app_install = "sample_app.utils.after_app_install"
before_app_uninstall = "sample_app.utils.before_app_uninstall"

before_migrate = "sample_app.migrate.before_migrate"
after_migrate = "sample_app.migrate.after_migrate"
Hook When it runs required_apps install-app installs these apps first. before_install Before the DocTypes of this app are synced. Return False to stop the install. after_install After the app is added to installed_apps. after_sync At the end of install, after fixtures and customizations are synced. before_app_install, after_app_install When any app is installed. The function gets the app name. before_uninstall, after_uninstall When this app is uninstalled. before_app_uninstall, after_app_uninstall When any app is uninstalled. The function gets the app name. before_migrate, after_migrate At the start and end of bench migrate.

See Apps for the full install order.

docs.title: Document events
docs.text:
doc_events runs functions on controller events of any DocType. The key is a DocType name, a tuple of names, or "*" for all DocTypes.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doc_events = {
    "Sample Order": {
        "validate": "sample_app.events.check_credit_limit",
        "on_submit": [
            "sample_app.events.notify_customer",
            "sample_app.events.update_stock",
        ],
    },
    ("Sample Item", "Sample Order"): {
        "on_trash": "sample_app.events.log_delete",
    },
    "*": {
        "on_update": "sample_app.events.audit",
    },
}

# sample_app/events.py
import frappe


def check_credit_limit(doc, method):
    if doc.total > 100000:
        frappe.throw(frappe._("Total is over the credit limit"))


def audit(doc):
    # the method argument is optional
    frappe.logger().info(f"{doc.doctype} {doc.name} updated")

The handler gets the document and the event name. For a handler with one positional parameter, Frappe passes only the document. Handlers run after the controller method. See Controllers for the event order.

Warning

Do not call frappe.db.commit() in a doc_events handler. Frappe ignores the call and shows a warning.

docs.title: Override and extend controllers
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
override_doctype_class = {
    "ToDo": "sample_app.overrides.todo.CustomToDo",
}

extend_doctype_class = {
    "ToDo": "sample_app.overrides.todo.ToDoMixin",
}

override_whitelisted_methods = {
    "frappe.desk.doctype.event.event.get_events": "sample_app.event.get_events",
}
Hook Rule override_doctype_class The class must be a subclass of the original controller. Frappe throws an error if it is not. extend_doctype_class Mixin classes. Frappe makes a new class with the mixins before the controller in the MRO. All apps' mixins apply. override_whitelisted_methods Requests to the original dotted path call the new function.

These hooks have no effect on custom DocTypes (custom = 1). Custom DocTypes always use Document or NestedSet. See Extending Apps.

docs.title: Desk and web assets
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
app_include_js = "sample_app.bundle.js"
app_include_css = "sample_app.bundle.css"
web_include_js = "sample_app_web.bundle.js"
web_include_css = "sample_app_web.bundle.css"

doctype_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo.js"}
doctype_list_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo_list.js"}
Hook Effect app_include_js, app_include_css Load in every desk page. web_include_js, web_include_css Load in every website page. doctype_js Add a form script to a DocType of another app. Path is relative to the app package. doctype_list_js, doctype_tree_js, doctype_calendar_js, doctype_kanban_js Add view scripts the same way.

See Form Scripts and List View Settings.

docs.title: Scheduled jobs
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
scheduler_events = {
    "daily": ["sample_app.tasks.send_reminders"],
    "cron": {
        "0/15 * * * *": ["sample_app.tasks.sync_orders"],
    },
}

See Scheduler.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
permission_query_conditions = {
    "Sample Order": "sample_app.permissions.sample_order_query",
}
has_permission = {
    "Sample Order": "sample_app.permissions.sample_order_has_permission",
}

See Permissions.

docs.title: Fixtures
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
fixtures = [
    "Sample Role",
    {"dt": "Custom Field", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]},
]

An entry is a DocType name or a dict with dt (or doctype), filters, or_filters and prefix. See Fixtures and Patches.

docs.title: Requests, sessions and templates
docs.text: Hook Shape Effect before_request, after_request list of dotted paths Run before and after each HTTP request. after_request functions get response and request. boot_session list of dotted paths Each function gets bootinfo and can add keys for the desk. extend_bootinfo list of dotted paths Each function gets bootinfo= as a keyword argument. jinja dict with methods and filters Add functions and filters to the Jinja environment. website_route_rules list of {"from_route", "to_route"} Map URL patterns to pages. See Website.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A hook value that is a function object, class or module is ignored. Always use a dotted path string.
  • Names that start with _ are not hooks. Use them for private helpers in hooks.py.
  • A typo in a hook key fails without an error. Frappe reads only the keys it knows.
  • Two apps that override the same DocType class do not both apply. Only the last one wins. install-app prints a warning for this case.
  • After you edit hooks.py, clear the cache and restart the bench processes.
