docs.title: Print Formats
docs.text: A Print Format decides how a document looks when printed, sent as a PDF, or attached to an email. Each Print Format document is linked to a DocType (doc_type) or to a report (print_format_for = "Report"). Users design most formats in the desk (see Printing (user guide)). As a developer you ship formats in your app, render them from code, and extend the PDF pipeline.

docs.title: Kinds of Print Format
docs.text:
Kind Fields Rendered by Standard No Print Format, or "Standard" Layout of the DocType form, frappe/www/printview.py Editor format print_format_builder_beta = 1, format_data (layout JSON) PrintFormatGenerator (frappe/utils/print_format_generator.py) Custom Jinja custom_format = 1, print_format_type = "Jinja", html get_rendered_template() in frappe/www/printview.py Raw printing custom_format = 1, raw_printing = 1, raw_commands Sent to a printer as raw commands

The classic Print Format Builder cannot create new formats. create_custom_format() in frappe/printing/doctype/print_format/print_format.py makes every new builder format with print_format_builder_beta = 1. Older formats that still have a classic layout keep rendering with the standard template. Prefer editor formats. Use a custom Jinja format only when the layout cannot be built from editor blocks.

docs.title: Print Formats in an app
docs.text:
Set standard to "Yes" and save in developer mode. export_doc() writes the JSON to the module folder. For a Jinja format, put the template in an .html file with the same name. get_print_format() reads that file before the html field.

sample_app/sample_app/selling/print_format/sample_order_slip/
├── sample_order_slip.json
└── sample_order_slip.html

{# sample_app/sample_app/selling/print_format/sample_order_slip/sample_order_slip.html #}
<h2>{{ doc.name }}</h2>
<p>{{ doc.customer_name }}, {{ doc.get_formatted("order_date") }}</p>
<table class="table table-bordered">
    {% for row in doc.items %}
    <tr>
        <td>{{ row.item }}</td>
        <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("qty") }}</td>
        <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("amount", doc) }}</td>
    </tr>
    {% endfor %}
</table>
<p class="text-right"><b>{{ _("Total") }}: {{ doc.get_formatted("total") }}</b></p>

Without developer mode, a standard Print Format cannot be saved ("Standard Print Format cannot be updated").

docs.title: Template context
docs.text:
get_rendered_template() renders the template with these variables:

Name Value doc The document. Use doc.get_formatted("<fieldname>") for values in the user's format. meta frappe.get_meta(doc.doctype) layout The form layout in sections and columns (make_layout) no_letterhead 1 when the letter head is off letter_head Rendered letter head HTML footer Rendered letter head footer HTML print_settings Print Settings as a dict trigger_print 1 when the page opens the print dialog

The Jinja globals of Website are also available, for example frappe.db.get_value and _. Methods and filters from the jinja hook work too. validate_template checks the Jinja when you save.

docs.title: Before print
docs.text:
Before it renders, Frappe sets doc.flags.in_print and calls the controller method before_print(settings). Use it to set values that only the print shows.

# sample_app/sample_app/selling/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
class SampleOrder(Document):
    def before_print(self, settings=None):
        self.print_heading = f"Order {self.name}"

docs.title: Render from code
docs.text:
frappe.get_print() returns HTML, or PDF bytes with as_pdf=True. It checks print permission for the current user.

html = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001")
pdf = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001", print_format="Sample Order Slip", as_pdf=True)

with open("/tmp/so-00001.pdf", "wb") as f:
    f.write(pdf)
Parameter Default Description doctype, name None The document to print. print_format None Print Format name. Empty uses the DocType default, then "Standard". style None Print Style name. Empty uses Print Settings print_style. as_pdf False Return PDF bytes instead of HTML. doc None A document object to print instead of loading it. no_letterhead 0 Leave out the letter head. letterhead None Letter Head name to use. password None Encrypt the PDF with this password. pdf_options None Options for the PDF engine. pdf_generator None "wkhtmltopdf", "chrome", "PlutoPrint", "Typst" or "WeasyPrint". Overrides the format and Print Settings for HTML formats. output None A pypdf.PdfWriter. Pages are added to it.

frappe.attach_print(doctype, name, print_format=None, ...) returns {"fname": ..., "fcontent": ...} for an email attachment. It returns a PDF when Print Settings send_print_as_pdf is on, else HTML. It skips the print permission check (frappe.local.flags.ignore_print_permissions).

frappe.translate.print_language("de") is a context manager that prints in another language.

docs.title: URLs
docs.text:
URL Returns /printview?doctype=Sample Order&name=SO-00001&format=Sample Order Slip HTML print view /Sample Order/SO-00001 HTML print view (PrintPage renderer) /api/method/frappe.utils.print_format.download_pdf?doctype=Sample Order&name=SO-00001&format=... PDF download /api/method/frappe.utils.print_format.download_multi_pdf One PDF for many documents

download_pdf takes doctype, name, format, no_letterhead, language, letterhead, pdf_generator, style and settings.

docs.title: PDF engines
docs.text:
pdf_generator on the Print Format picks the engine. Print Settings pdf_generator is the default for formats that do not set one. Print Settings offers wkhtmltopdf, chrome and PlutoPrint. Its field default is chrome.

Value Description wkhtmltopdf Renders HTML with the wkhtmltopdf binary (frappe.utils.pdf.get_pdf()). Install it on the server. The fallback when nothing else is set. chrome Renders HTML with a headless Chromium (frappe/utils/pdf_generator/). bench setup-chrome downloads it. PlutoPrint Renders HTML without a browser process. Falls back to chrome when PlutoPrint is not installed or the format has JavaScript or CSS grid (plutoprint_blockers). get_plutoprint_pdf() also uses chrome for a page range. Typst Editor formats only, without custom CSS in the Style box. typst_blockers() in frappe/utils/typst_emitter.py lists what stops it. WeasyPrint Deprecated. Kept only for editor formats that already use it. A new format cannot select it.

resolve_pdf_generator() in frappe/utils/print_utils.py picks the engine:

  1. For an editor format, it keeps Typst, WeasyPrint or PlutoPrint (when PlutoPrint can render it). Otherwise it uses chrome.
  2. For other formats, it uses the pdf_generator argument, then the format's pdf_generator, then Print Settings pdf_generator, then wkhtmltopdf.
  3. It changes PlutoPrint to chrome when PlutoPrint cannot render the format.

Version

The patch frappe/patches/v16_0/set_weasyprint_generator_for_beta_formats.py sets existing editor formats to WeasyPrint, so they render as before. WeasyPrint shows a deprecation warning. Switch these formats to chrome. Later versions remove WeasyPrint and wkhtmltopdf.

docs.title: The pdf_generator hook
docs.text:
For an HTML format, get_print(as_pdf=True) renders the HTML. If the engine is not wkhtmltopdf, it calls each function in the pdf_generator hook. The first one that returns bytes wins. If none returns a value, Frappe uses frappe.utils.pdf.get_pdf(), which runs wkhtmltopdf.

# frappe/hooks.py
pdf_generator = [
    "frappe.utils.pdf.get_chrome_pdf",
    "frappe.utils.pdf.get_plutoprint_pdf",
    "frappe.utils.print_format_generator.get_typst_pdf",
    "frappe.utils.weasyprint.get_weasyprint_pdf",
]

To add an engine:

  1. Add your engine name to the options of the pdf_generator field of Print Format and Print Settings, for example with a Property Setter in your fixtures.
  2. Add a function to the pdf_generator hook.
  3. In the function, return None when pdf_generator is not your engine.
# sample_app/hooks.py
pdf_generator = ["sample_app.pdf.get_sample_pdf"]

# sample_app/pdf.py
def get_sample_pdf(print_format, html, options, output, pdf_generator=None):
    if pdf_generator != "Sample Engine":
        return None
    return render_with_sample_engine(html, options)  # must return PDF bytes

docs.title: Other print hooks
docs.text: Hook Called with Use on_print_pdf doctype, name, print_format Run code before a PDF is made, for example to log it. get_print_format_template jenv, print_format Return a compiled Jinja template to use instead of the format's HTML. The last app wins. pdf_body_html jenv, template, print_format, args Render the body HTML. Frappe sets frappe.utils.pdf.pdf_body_html. The last app wins. pdf_header_html, pdf_footer_html soup, head, content, styles, html_id, css Build the repeating header and footer.

docs.title: Letter heads
docs.text: get_letter_head() uses, in order: the letterhead argument, the document's letter_head field, then the Letter Head with is_default = 1. When neither argument is passed, Print Settings with_letterhead decides. Frappe renders the letter head content and footer with Jinja and {"doc": doc.as_dict()}, so you can use {{ doc.customer_name }} in a letter head.

docs.title: Print styles
docs.text: Frappe renders templates/styles/standard.css, then adds the css of the selected Print Style, then the Print Settings font_size. A Jinja format can add CSS in its css field. Frappe ships the styles in frappe/printing/print_style/.

docs.title: Raw printing
docs.text: A raw format sends printer commands (for example ESC/POS or ZPL) instead of HTML. Set raw_printing and write the commands in raw_commands with Jinja. frappe.www.printview.get_rendered_raw_commands(doc, name, print_format) returns the rendered commands. The desk sends them to the printer through QZ Tray when Print Settings enable_raw_printing is on.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A draft document of a submittable DocType prints only when Print Settings allow_print_for_draft is on. A cancelled one needs allow_print_for_cancelled.
  • Fields with print_hide and fields above the user's permission level are not printed.
  • Use get_formatted() instead of raw values. Raw values do not follow the user's date, number and currency format.
  • Render every format and look at the PDF before you ship it. wkhtmltopdf, PlutoPrint and Chromium can break pages differently.
  • wkhtmltopdf does not use the print_font print setting. get_print() removes it.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
A report is a Report document. Its report_type decides how it gets data. Use a Script Report when you need Python logic, joins or computed columns. Use a Query Report for one SQL query. Report Builder and Custom Report are saved views that users make in the desk. For the desk side, see Reports (user guide).

report_type Data comes from Made by Report Builder A saved list view of ref_doctype (json field) Users, in Report view Query Report The SQL in query Developers or System Managers Script Report execute(filters) in a Python file (standard) or report_script (not standard) Developers Custom Report A saved copy of a Query or Script Report with its own columns and filters Users, with "Save As"

docs.title: Script Report in an app
docs.text:
A standard Script Report (is_standard = "Yes") lives in the module folder of the app.

sample_app/sample_app/selling/report/sample_order_summary/
├── __init__.py
├── sample_order_summary.json   # the Report document
├── sample_order_summary.py     # execute(filters)
└── sample_order_summary.js     # filters and client options
  1. Turn on developer_mode in site config.
  2. Log in as Administrator.
  3. Create a Report with report_type "Script Report", ref_doctype "Sample Order" and a module of your app.
  4. Save. In developer mode, Frappe sets is_standard to "Yes" and writes the JSON, .py and .js boilerplate.
  5. Fill in the .py and .js files.
  6. Commit the folder. bench migrate syncs the report to other sites.

Frappe finds the module as <app>.<module>.report.<report_name>.<report_name> (get_report_module_dotted_path).

docs.title: The Python file
docs.text:
execute(filters) gets the filter values as a frappe._dict and returns a tuple or list. Frappe reads up to six items, in this order:

Position Name Type Description 0 columns list Column definitions. Dicts or strings. 1 data list Rows. Each row is a dict (keys are column fieldname) or a list in column order. 2 message str HTML shown above the table. 3 chart dict Chart shown above the table. 4 report_summary list Number cards shown above the table. 5 skip_total_row bool Do not add the total row for this run. 
# sample_app/sample_app/selling/report/sample_order_summary/sample_order_summary.py
import frappe
from frappe import _


def execute(filters=None):
    filters = frappe._dict(filters or {})
    columns = get_columns()
    data = get_data(filters)
    return columns, data, None, get_chart(data), get_summary(data)


def get_columns():
    return [
        {"label": _("Order"), "fieldname": "name", "fieldtype": "Link", "options": "Sample Order", "width": 140},
        {"label": _("Customer"), "fieldname": "customer_name", "fieldtype": "Data", "width": 180},
        {"label": _("Order Date"), "fieldname": "order_date", "fieldtype": "Date", "width": 110},
        {"label": _("Status"), "fieldname": "status", "fieldtype": "Data", "width": 100},
        {"label": _("Total"), "fieldname": "total", "fieldtype": "Currency", "width": 120},
    ]


def get_data(filters):
    conditions = {"docstatus": ["<", 2]}
    if filters.status:
        conditions["status"] = filters.status
    if filters.from_date and filters.to_date:
        conditions["order_date"] = ["between", [filters.from_date, filters.to_date]]

    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Order",
        filters=conditions,
        fields=["name", "customer_name", "order_date", "status", "total"],
        order_by="order_date desc",
    )


def get_chart(data):
    return {
        "data": {
            "labels": [row.name for row in data],
            "datasets": [{"name": _("Total"), "values": [row.total for row in data]}],
        },
        "type": "bar",
    }


def get_summary(data):
    return [
        {"label": _("Orders"), "value": len(data), "datatype": "Int"},
        {"label": _("Total"), "value": sum(row.total for row in data), "datatype": "Currency", "indicator": "Green"},
    ]

A column can also be a string in the form "Label:Fieldtype/Options:Width", for example "Order:Link/Sample Order:150". Frappe converts it to a dict and makes the fieldname from the label.

The chart dict goes to Frappe Charts: data.labels, data.datasets[].name, data.datasets[].values, and type (for example bar, line, pie, percentage, axis-mixed). A summary item has label, value and datatype. It can also have indicator (Green, Red, Blue and other colors) and currency.

The module can also define these functions:

Function Used for execute_snapshot_report(filters) Called instead of execute when the report has snapshot_report set. get_xlsx_styles(metadata) Styles for the Excel export.

Report.get_module_method() allows only these two names and execute.

docs.title: The JS file
docs.text:
The .js file sets frappe.query_reports["<Report Name>"]. The key must be the report name.

// sample_app/sample_app/selling/report/sample_order_summary/sample_order_summary.js
frappe.query_reports["Sample Order Summary"] = {
    filters: [
        {
            fieldname: "status",
            label: __("Status"),
            fieldtype: "Select",
            options: ["", "Draft", "Open", "Completed"],
        },
        {
            fieldname: "from_date",
            label: __("From Date"),
            fieldtype: "Date",
            default: frappe.datetime.add_months(frappe.datetime.get_today(), -1),
        },
        {
            fieldname: "to_date",
            label: __("To Date"),
            fieldtype: "Date",
            default: frappe.datetime.get_today(),
        },
    ],
    formatter(value, row, column, data, default_formatter) {
        value = default_formatter(value, row, column, data);
        if (column.fieldname === "status" && data && data.status === "Open") {
            value = `<b>${value}</b>`;
        }
        return value;
    },
    onload(report) {
        report.page.add_inner_button(__("Refresh"), () => report.refresh());
    },
};

A filter is a field definition (fieldname, label, fieldtype, options, default, reqd, depends_on, on_change, get_query). Read a value with frappe.query_report.get_filter_value("status"). Set one with frappe.query_report.set_filter_value("status", "Open").

Other keys that the report view reads: onload, formatter, get_datatable_options, after_datatable_render, after_refresh, get_chart_data, get_pdf_format, tree, parent_field, initial_depth, collapsible_filters, separate_check_filters, export_hidden_cols. A <report_name>.html file in the report folder is the print template of the report.

docs.title: Filters table
docs.text: The Report has a filters table (Report Filter) with fieldname, label, fieldtype, options, mandatory, default and wildcard_filter. The desk uses these rows only when the JS file does not set filters. Frappe does not check the filter values on the server. Check them in execute.

docs.title: Script Report without a file
docs.text: A Script Report with is_standard = "No" runs report_script with safe_exec. Only a Script Manager can save it, and server scripts must be on (see Server and Client Scripts). The script gets filters. It sets data (a full result like the return value of execute) or result (rows only, with columns from the columns table).

docs.title: Query Report
docs.text:
A Query Report runs query with the filter values as SQL parameters. Write the column definition as the column alias.

select
    name as "Order:Link/Sample Order:150",
    customer_name as "Customer::150",
    total as "Total:Currency:120"
from `tabSample Order`
where docstatus < 2
    and customer_name like %(customer)s

execute_query_report() checks the query with check_safe_sql_query, then runs it with frappe.db.sql. The filters in the JS file (or the filters table) give the values for %(customer)s. The result rows come back as dicts, with fieldname made from the label (order, customer, total).

docs.title: Run a report from code
docs.text:
frappe.desk.query_report.run is the method that the desk calls. It is whitelisted and read-only.

from frappe.desk.query_report import run

result = run("Sample Order Summary", filters={"status": "Open"})
result["columns"]   # list of column dicts
result["result"]    # list of row dicts, plus a total row (a list) when add_total_row is set

The returned dict has result, columns, message, chart, report_summary, skip_total_row, status, execution_time and add_total_row. A snapshot report also has snapshot_report and snapshot_at. For a prepared report, it has prepared_report and doc and the saved result.

curl -b cookies.txt -G "http://<site>/api/method/frappe.desk.query_report.run" \
  --data-urlencode 'report_name=Sample Order Summary' \
  --data-urlencode 'filters={"status": "Open"}'
Parameter Type Default Description report_name str required Name of the Report. filters dict or JSON str None Filter values. ignore_prepared_report bool False Run now, also for a prepared report. custom_columns list None Extra columns from linked DocTypes. is_tree, parent_field bool, str False, None Build the total row for a tree report. are_default_filters bool True Use the saved filters of a Custom Report. js_filters list None Filter definitions from the client, used to check Link filter permissions.

docs.title: Permissions and roles
docs.text:
get_report_doc() checks these before a run:

  1. Report.is_permitted(). The user must have one of the roles in the roles table. A Custom Role for the report replaces that table. When no roles are set, all users are allowed.
  2. The user has report permission on ref_doctype.
  3. The report is not disabled.

A new report that is not standard gets the permlevel 0 roles of ref_doctype in roles (set_doctype_roles). After the run, get_filtered_data() removes rows with Link values that the user's user permissions do not allow. Still check permissions in execute. Use frappe.get_list, or frappe.only_for("System Manager") for admin reports.

docs.title: Prepared reports
docs.text:
A prepared report runs in a background job and saves the result in a Prepared Report document with a file attachment. Use it for slow reports.

  • Set prepared_report on the Report to always run it in the background.
  • A Script Report that runs for more than 15 seconds turns on prepared_report by itself. Set disable_prepared_report_automation to stop this.
  • The job runs on the long queue. timeout on the Report sets the job timeout. The default is 1500 seconds (REPORT_TIMEOUT).
  • run() returns the last completed result for the same filters and user. Users start a new run with "Generate New Report" (frappe.core.doctype.prepared_report.prepared_report.make_prepared_report).
  • The user gets a notification when the job is done.
  • If the job fails, Frappe sets the Prepared Report status to "Error" and saves the traceback in error_message.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• run() has @frappe.read_only. With read_from_replica in site config, it reads from the replica. Do not write to the database in execute.
  • Use the same fieldname in columns and row dicts. Rows with other keys show empty cells.
  • A Query Report cannot skip a condition when a filter is empty. Use a Script Report for optional filters.
  • add_total_row adds a list row at the end of result. Code that reads result must handle it.
  • The report name, the folder name and the JS key must match. The folder name is the scrubbed report name.

docs.title: Jobs, Realtime and Caching
docs.text:
Run background jobs and scheduled tasks, push realtime events and cache data.

Page What it covers Background Jobs Run code outside the web request with frappe.enqueue and enqueue_doc, on RQ queues served by bench workers. Scheduler Run functions on a schedule with the scheduler_events hook, Scheduled Job Type records and the bench schedule process. Realtime Push events from the server to browsers with publish_realtime, Socket.IO rooms and frappe.realtime.on, and add custom realtime handlers. Caching Cache data in Redis with frappe.cache, read documents with get_cached_doc and get_cached_value, and use the request_cache, site_cache and redis_cache decorators.

docs.title: Background Jobs
docs.text: Use a background job when work takes longer than a web request should wait: bulk updates, imports, reports, emails, calls to slow external services. Frappe puts the job on a Redis queue (RQ). A worker process (bench worker) takes the job and runs it in a fresh site context. Use frappe.enqueue for a function and frappe.enqueue_doc for a controller method.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
• Queue: a named RQ queue. Frappe has three built-in queues: short, default and long. You can add more in common_site_config.json (see Queues and timeouts).
  • Worker: a process that takes jobs from one or more queues. Start it with bench worker. In production, supervisor or systemd runs the workers (see Deployment).
  • Job ID: every job has an ID. Frappe adds the site name as a prefix, so the ID my_job becomes <site>||my_job. If you do not give an ID, RQ makes a UUID.
  • RQ Job: a virtual DocType that shows jobs in Redis. Open it at /desk/rq-job. It shows the status (queued, started, finished, failed, deferred, scheduled, canceled), arguments, timeout and exception.

docs.title: Enqueue a function
docs.text:
# sample_app/sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def recalculate_rates(category: str):
    frappe.only_for("System Manager")
    frappe.enqueue(
        "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.recalculate_item_rates",
        queue="long",
        timeout=1800,
        category=category,  # passed to the job as a keyword argument
    )

# sample_app/sample_app/jobs.py
import frappe


def recalculate_item_rates(category: str):
    for name in frappe.get_all("Sample Item", {"category": category}, pluck="name"):
        item = frappe.get_doc("Sample Item", name)
        item.rate = item.rate * 1.1
        item.save()

You can pass the dotted path as a string or the function object. All extra keyword arguments go to the function. They must be picklable.

What the worker does for each job (execute_job in frappe/utils/background_jobs.py):

  1. Connects to the site and sets the user to the user who enqueued the job (frappe.session.user at enqueue time).
  2. Sets frappe.job with site, method, job_name, kwargs and user.
  3. Runs every before_job hook.
  4. Runs the function.
  5. Commits the transaction if the function returns. Rolls back, writes an Error Log and raises again if it fails.
  6. Runs every after_job hook.

The job does not check permissions for you. The job runs with the roles of the user who enqueued it, so check permissions in the whitelisted method before you enqueue.

docs.title: Retries on deadlock
docs.text:
If the function raises a deadlock, a lock wait timeout, or frappe.RetryBackgroundJobError, the worker rolls back and runs the function again. It tries up to 5 more times and waits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 seconds between attempts. frappe.enqueue has no other retry option in v16.

Warning

In v16 a retried attempt does not get the user of the first attempt. The site connects as Administrator for the retry. Do not depend on frappe.session.user in a job that can raise frappe.RetryBackgroundJobError.

docs.title: Enqueue after commit
docs.text:
When the job reads a document that the current request creates, enqueue it after commit. Otherwise the worker can start before the data is in the database.

def on_submit(self):
    frappe.enqueue(
        "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.notify_order",
        order=self.name,
        enqueue_after_commit=True,
    )

With enqueue_after_commit=True, frappe.enqueue returns None. If the transaction rolls back, the job is not queued.

docs.title: Deduplicate jobs
docs.text:
Give a job_id and set deduplicate=True to skip the call when the same job is queued or running.

frappe.enqueue(
    "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.rebuild_index",
    queue="long",
    job_id="sample_rebuild_index",
    deduplicate=True,
)

If a job with that ID is queued or started, frappe.enqueue writes a log line and returns None. If a finished or failed job with that ID exists, Frappe deletes it and queues a new one. deduplicate=True without job_id raises an error.

Check a job from code:

from frappe.utils.background_jobs import get_job_status, is_job_enqueued

is_job_enqueued("sample_rebuild_index")  # True while queued or started
get_job_status("sample_rebuild_index")   # rq JobStatus, or None if not found

Pass the ID without the site prefix. These functions add it.

docs.title: Run a controller method in the background
docs.text:
frappe.enqueue_doc loads the document in the worker and calls one of its methods.

frappe.enqueue_doc("Sample Order", "SO-0001", "send_reminders", queue="short", timeout=300)

The worker calls frappe.get_doc(doctype, name).<method>(**kwargs). The default timeout of enqueue_doc is 300 seconds.

docs.title: The frappe.task decorator
docs.text:
@frappe.task(...) adds an enqueue attribute to a function. The decorator arguments become frappe.enqueue arguments.

@frappe.task(queue="long", timeout=1800)
def rebuild_index(category=None):
    ...


rebuild_index.enqueue(category="Hardware")

docs.title: Show progress to the user
docs.text: v16 has no task DocType for user-facing jobs. To show progress, call frappe.publish_progress in the job. See Realtime.

docs.title: frappe.enqueue parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Default Description method str or callable required Function to run. queue str "default" Queue name. Must be a known queue, or frappe.enqueue raises ValidationError. timeout int queue timeout Seconds before RQ stops the job. event str None Label stored with the job. Used by bench purge-jobs --event. is_async bool True False runs the job in the current process. Deprecated outside tests, use now. job_name str None Deprecated. Use job_id. now bool False Run the function now with frappe.call, in the current process and transaction. enqueue_after_commit bool False Queue the job only after the current transaction commits. on_success callable None RQ success callback. on_failure callable truncate_failed_registry RQ failure callback. at_front bool False Put the job at the front of the queue. job_id str UUID Job ID. Frappe adds <site>|| before it. deduplicate bool False Do not queue if a job with job_id is queued or started. at_front_when_starved bool False Put the job at the front when more than 16 jobs wait in the queue. **kwargs Arguments for the function.

All parameters after enqueue_after_commit are keyword-only. Return value: the rq.job.Job. It is None when the job is deduplicated or queued after commit. With now=True, it is the return value of the function.

docs.title: Queues and timeouts
Workers and CLI
docs.text:
Command Description bench worker Start a worker for all queues. bench worker --queue short,default Start a worker for some queues. Other options: --burst (exit when the queues are empty), --strategy round_robin\|random, --quiet, -u/--rq-username, -p/--rq-password. bench worker-pool --num-workers 4 Start a pool of workers (experimental). The default is 2 workers. bench doctor Show scheduler status and the number of workers online. bench --site <site> show-pending-jobs Show jobs that wait in the queues. bench purge-jobs --site <site> [--queue] [--event] Delete pending jobs.

Workers run with a lower CPU priority than web processes. The default niceness increment is 10. Change it with background_process_niceness in common_site_config.json.

docs.title: Configuration keys
docs.text: Key Default Description workers none Extra queues and their timeouts. common_site_config.json only. max_queued_jobs 500 Queue size at which frappe.enqueue fails. rq_job_failure_ttl 7 days Seconds to keep failed jobs in Redis. rq_results_ttl 600 Seconds to keep finished job results in Redis. rq_failed_jobs_limit 1000 Maximum number of failed jobs kept per queue. background_process_niceness 10 CPU niceness increment for workers and the scheduler. use_rq_auth, rq_username, rq_password off Connect to the queue Redis with an ACL user.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not pass documents or open files as arguments. Pass names and load the data in the job.
  • A job that runs with now=True shares the caller's transaction. It does not commit.
  • The worker commits only when the job ends. A long loop holds its writes until then. Commit in batches if you must, with frappe.db.commit().
  • Code changes do not reach running workers. Restart the workers after you deploy.
  • If you call frappe.db.commit() and then read in the same process, MariaDB can show you an old snapshot. Commit or roll back again before you read data that a worker wrote.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: Use a cache when your code reads the same data many times and the data changes rarely: settings, master records, computed lookups. Frappe has a Redis cache shared by all processes of the bench (frappe.cache), helpers that cache whole documents in it, and decorators that cache function results per request, per process or in Redis. Pick the smallest scope that works, and always plan how the cache gets cleared.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text: Tool Stored in Lives Shared across processes @request_cache frappe.local.request_cache One request or job No @site_cache Process memory Until ttl or clear_cache() No frappe.cache / @redis_cache Redis (redis_cache URL) Until expiry or delete Yes frappe.get_cached_doc / get_cached_value Redis 1 hour, or until the document is saved Yes frappe.client_cache Process memory + Redis 10 minutes local, invalidated by Redis Yes (internal use)

docs.title: frappe.cache
docs.text:
frappe.cache is a RedisWrapper (a subclass of redis.Redis). Values are pickled, so you can store dicts, lists and documents.

frappe.cache.set_value("sample_app:rates", {"Hardware": 10}, expires_in_sec=3600)
rates = frappe.cache.get_value("sample_app:rates")

# compute and store the value when it is missing
rates = frappe.cache.get_value("sample_app:rates", generator=load_rates)

frappe.cache.delete_value("sample_app:rates")
frappe.cache.delete_keys("sample_app:")  # every key that starts with the prefix

Keys are namespaced by site. frappe.cache.make_key("k") returns the key <db_name>|k as bytes. Options on most methods:

  • user=True adds user:<current user>: to the key. Pass a user ID to use another user.
  • shared=True uses the key as given, with no site prefix. All sites on the bench see it.
Method Description set_value(key, val, user=None, expires_in_sec=None, shared=False) Store a value. Returns the size in bytes. get_value(key, generator=None, user=None, expires=False, shared=False) Read a value. Calls generator on a miss and stores the result. delete_value(keys, user=None, make_keys=True, shared=False) Delete one key or a list of keys. delete_keys(key) Delete all keys that start with key. get_keys(key) List keys that start with key. exists(*names, user=None, shared=None) Count of keys that exist. expire_key(key, time) Set a TTL in seconds. hset(name, key, value), hget(name, key, generator=None), hdel(name, keys), hgetall(name) Hash operations, with the site prefix. lpush, rpush, lpop, rpop, llen, lrange, ltrim, sadd, srem, smembers List and set operations.

get_value also keeps the value in frappe.local.cache for the rest of the request. A second read in the same request does not go to Redis. Pass expires=True for keys with a TTL so the local copy is not kept.

If Redis is not reachable, set_value and get_value do not raise. get_value returns None, or the generator result.

Deprecated

frappe.cache() (called as a function) is deprecated. Use frappe.cache.

docs.title: Cached documents
docs.text:
settings = frappe.get_cached_doc("System Settings")
item = frappe.get_cached_doc("Sample Item", "Laptop")
rate = frappe.get_cached_value("Sample Item", "Laptop", "rate")
values = frappe.get_cached_value("User", "user1@example.com", ["first_name", "user_type"], as_dict=True)
time_zone = frappe.get_single_value("System Settings", "time_zone")
  • get_cached_doc takes the same arguments as frappe.get_doc. It stores the document in Redis for 1 hour under document_cache::<doctype>::<name>.
  • Saving or deleting the document clears its cache entry (Document.clear_cache). The entry is cleared again after commit and after rollback.
  • Clear it yourself with frappe.clear_document_cache(doctype, name). Without name, it clears all cached documents of the DocType.
  • get_cached_value returns None if the document does not exist.
  • frappe.get_single_value(doctype, fieldname) reads a field of a Single DocType through get_cached_value.
  • These functions do not check permissions.

Warning

frappe.db.set_value and frappe.db.set_single_value clear the document cache. Raw SQL (frappe.db.sql) and frappe.qb updates do not. After such writes, call frappe.clear_document_cache.

docs.title: Decorators
docs.text: All three are in frappe.utils.caching. frappe.request_cache and frappe.site_cache are aliases.

docs.title: request_cache
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.caching import request_cache


@request_cache
def get_item_rate(item: str) -> float:
    return frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", item, "rate")

Calls with the same arguments in one request or job run once. Arguments must be hashable. Unhashable arguments skip the cache.

docs.title: site_cache
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.caching import site_cache


@site_cache(ttl=300, maxsize=128)
def get_category_map() -> dict:
    return dict(frappe.get_all("Sample Item", fields=["name", "category"], as_list=True))


get_category_map.clear_cache()  # clear for all sites in this process

The key includes the site, so sites do not share results. The cache is per process: each web worker and background worker has its own copy, and clear_cache() only clears the current process. frappe.clear_cache() clears all site_cache entries in the current process. When maxsize is reached, the oldest entry is removed.

docs.title: redis_cache
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.caching import redis_cache


@redis_cache(ttl=600)
def get_open_order_count(customer: str) -> int:
    return frappe.db.count("Sample Order", {"customer_name": customer, "status": "Open"})


get_open_order_count.clear_cache()
Argument Default Description ttl 3600 Seconds to keep each result. user None True caches one result for each session user. shared False True shares the results across sites.

The cache key is <module>.<function>::<hash of arguments>. clear_cache() deletes every result of the function. A None result is cached too.

docs.title: http_cache
docs.text: @http_cache(public=False, max_age=None, stale_while_revalidate=None) sets a Cache-Control header on GET responses of a whitelisted method. It does not cache on the server.

docs.title: client_cache
docs.text: frappe.client_cache keeps hot keys in process memory and uses Redis client-side caching to invalidate them. Frappe uses it for hooks, schema and settings. The docstring says it is internal and can change without notice. Use frappe.cache in apps. It has get_value, set_value, delete_value, delete_keys and get_doc. The local TTL is 10 minutes and the default size is 1024 keys. client_cache_max_bytes in site config limits its memory.

docs.title: Clear the cache
docs.text:
bench --site frappe.localhost clear-cache
bench --site frappe.localhost clear-website-cache

frappe.clear_cache()                       # all site keys, site_cache, client_cache
frappe.clear_cache(doctype="Sample Item")  # DocType meta and related caches
frappe.clear_cache(user="user1@example.com")  # user caches (roles, permissions, defaults)

A full frappe.clear_cache() deletes all Redis keys of the site except keys that match the persistent_cache_keys hook. Then it runs every clear_cache hook.

# sample_app/hooks.py
persistent_cache_keys = ["sample_app:rates*"]  # kept by frappe.clear_cache()
clear_cache = "sample_app.cache.clear_sample_cache"  # called by frappe.clear_cache()

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Never cache data that depends on permissions in a key that other users can read. Use user=True.
  • Changes from site_cache do not reach other processes. Do not use it for data that users edit.
  • Cached documents are copies. Changing a cached document does not change the database. Use frappe.get_doc when you will save.
  • Do not cache large values in client_cache. It is sized for values of about 4 KB.

docs.title: Realtime
docs.text: Use realtime events to push data from the server to open browser tabs: a progress bar, a refresh after a background job, a message to one user. Server code calls frappe.publish_realtime. Frappe publishes the event on the Redis channel events. The Socket.IO server (bench socketio) reads the channel and sends the event to the browsers in the target room. Browser code listens with frappe.realtime.on.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
• Event: a name, such as doc_update or sample_order_ready, and a JSON message.
  • Room: a group of sockets on one site. The server sends each event to one room.
  • Socket.IO server: a separate process. It listens on socketio_port (default 9000). There are two backends: the Node server apps/frappe/socketio.js and the Python server python -m frappe.realtime.server. The bench socketio command picks one from the socketio_backend key in common_site_config.json (node by default, or python).

docs.title: Rooms
docs.text:
Room Who is in it How a socket joins user:<user> All sockets of that user on the site On connect website All sockets on the site, guests too On connect all Sockets of System Users on the site On connect doctype:<doctype> Sockets that show a list of that DocType doctype_subscribe, needs read permission doc:<doctype>/<name> Sockets that have the form open doc_subscribe, needs read permission open_doc:<doctype>/<name> Sockets that view the form now. Used for doc_viewers. doc_open task_progress:<task_id> Sockets that follow a task task_subscribe

The desk subscribes for you. A form subscribes to its document on load. A list view subscribes to its DocType.

docs.title: Publish from the server
docs.text:
frappe.publish_realtime(
    event="sample_order_ready",
    message={"order": "SO-0001", "status": "Ready"},
    user="user1@example.com",
    after_commit=True,
)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Default Description event str "task_progress" if a task ID is set, else "global" Event name. message dict {} JSON message. room str see below Room name. Overrides the other targets. user str None Send to the room user:<user>. doctype, docname str None Send to the room doc:<doctype>/<docname>. task_id str frappe.local.task_id Send to the room task_progress:<task_id>. Forces after_commit=False. after_commit bool False Send only after the transaction commits. Dropped on rollback. Duplicate events are sent once.

When room is not given, the first match wins: task_id, then user, then doctype and docname. If none is given, the event goes to the all room (System Users of the site).

Special cases:

  • msgprint without user goes to the current user.
  • list_update always goes to doctype:<doctype>. The DocType comes from doctype or from message["doctype"].
  • docinfo_update always goes to doc:<doctype>/<docname>.

Use after_commit=True when the browser reloads data after the event. Otherwise the browser can read the database before your changes are committed.

docs.title: Named helpers
docs.text:
frappe.realtime has one helper for each room. Each calls publish_realtime and takes after_commit as a keyword-only argument.

from frappe.realtime import (
    publish_task_progress,
    publish_to_all,
    publish_to_doc,
    publish_to_doctype,
    publish_to_room,
    publish_to_user,
    publish_to_website,
)

publish_to_doc("Sample Order", "SO-0001", "sample_order_ready", {"status": "Ready"}, after_commit=True)
publish_to_doctype("Sample Order", "sample_orders_changed")
publish_to_room("doc:Sample Order/SO-0001", "sample_order_ready")

publish_task_progress(task_id, message) has no event argument. It sends task_progress.

docs.title: Progress bars
docs.text:
frappe.publish_progress sends the progress event. The desk shows a progress dialog.

def import_items(rows):
    for i, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
        ...
        frappe.publish_progress(i * 100 / len(rows), title="Importing items", description=f"Row {i}")

Signature: publish_progress(percent, title=None, doctype=None, docname=None, description=None, task_id=None). With doctype and docname, everyone with the form open sees the progress. Without them, only the current user sees it.

Call it from a background job to show the progress of long work.

docs.title: Events the framework sends
docs.text:
Event Room When Message doc_update doc:<doctype>/<name> After a document is saved (notify_update), after commit doctype, name, modified list_update doctype:<doctype> Same, for DocTypes that are not single, child or read-only doctype, name, user docinfo_update doc:<doctype>/<name> A Comment or Communication on the document changes varies doc_viewers open_doc:<doctype>/<name> A user opens or closes the form doctype, docname, users msgprint user:<user> frappe.msgprint(..., realtime=True) message progress user or doc room frappe.publish_progress percent, title, description

notify_update does not send events during import, patch, migrate and install. doc.db_set(..., notify=True) also calls it.

docs.title: From the CLI
docs.text:
bench --site frappe.localhost publish-realtime sample_event --message '{"status": "Open"}' --user Administrator

Options: --message, --room, --user, --doctype, --docname, --after-commit. The message is sent as a string.

docs.title: Listen in the browser
docs.text:
// sample_app/public/js/sample_order.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    refresh(frm) {
        frappe.realtime.off("sample_order_ready");
        frappe.realtime.on("sample_order_ready", (data) => {
            if (data.order === frm.doc.name) {
                frm.reload_doc();
            }
        });
    },
});

Client API (frappe.realtime, also frappe.socketio):

Method Description on(event, callback) Listen for an event. Connects the socket if needed. off(event, callback) Stop listening. Without callback, removes all listeners for the event. emit(event, ...args) Send an event to the server. doctype_subscribe(doctype) / doctype_unsubscribe(doctype) Join or leave doctype:<doctype>. doc_subscribe(doctype, name) / doc_unsubscribe(doctype, name) Join or leave doc:<doctype>/<name>. task_subscribe(task_id) / task_unsubscribe(task_id) Join or leave task_progress:<task_id>.

If disable_async is set in site config, the client does not connect.

Note

In v16 the client does not join its DocType and document rooms again after a reconnect. A list or form that was open during a Socket.IO restart can miss list_update and doc_update events. Reload the page to subscribe again.

docs.title: Custom handlers (Python backend)
docs.text:
With the Python backend, an app can handle events that the browser emits. Put the handlers in <app>/realtime/handlers.py. The server imports this module for each installed app at startup. A handler runs only for sockets on sites where its app is installed.

# sample_app/sample_app/realtime/handlers.py
from frappe.realtime import Socket, realtime


@realtime.on("sample_order_subscribe")
async def sample_order_subscribe(socket: Socket, order: str) -> dict:
    allowed = await socket.has_permission("Sample Order", order)
    if allowed:
        await socket.join(f"sample_order:{order}")
    return {"subscribed": allowed}

frappe.realtime.emit("sample_order_subscribe", "SO-0001");

Then publish to the same room from server code: publish_to_room("sample_order:SO-0001", "sample_order_ready", {...}).

Rules:

  • The first argument is the Socket. The other arguments are what the client sent.
  • The return value answers the client's acknowledgement callback.
  • @realtime.on(event, frappe_context=False, allow_guest=False). With allow_guest=False, events from guests are dropped.
  • Write handlers as async def. A plain def handler runs in a worker thread and gets a blocking socket with the same methods without await.
  • frappe_context=True opens a site context with a database connection for each event. It needs a plain def handler. Use it only when you must query the database.
  • An import error in handlers.py stops the server at startup.

Socket attributes: site, user, user_type, installed_apps. Methods: join(room), leave(room), emit(event, data=None, room=None), has_permission(doctype, name=None), set(key, value), get(key, default=None). has_permission calls the web process over HTTP.

docs.title: Configuration keys
docs.text:
All keys are in common_site_config.json.

Key Default Description socketio_port 9000 Port of the Socket.IO server. socketio_backend node node or python. Read by bench socketio. socketio_uds none Listen on this Unix socket instead of the port. socketio_worker_threads 4 Threads for blocking work in the Python server. redis_queue redis://127.0.0.1:11311 Redis that carries the events channel.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Events are not stored. A browser that is not connected when you publish misses the event.
  • A user sees events in user:<user> and all without a permission check. Do not put data there that the user must not read.
  • publish_realtime does nothing if Redis is down. It does not raise.
  • In a background job, publish after your writes commit, or use after_commit=True.

docs.title: Scheduler
docs.text: Use the scheduler to run a function at fixed times: each few minutes, hourly, daily, or on a cron expression. You declare the function in the scheduler_events hook of your app. Frappe stores each entry as a Scheduled Job Type record. The bench schedule process checks these records and puts due jobs on a background queue. A worker then runs them.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. bench migrate (and app install) reads scheduler_events from every installed app. It creates or updates one Scheduled Job Type per method, and deletes records whose method is no longer in the hooks.
  2. The bench schedule process wakes up each 4 minutes by default (scheduler_tick_interval).
  3. For each site, it skips the site if the scheduler is inactive (see Enable and disable).
  4. For each Scheduled Job Type that is not stopped, it computes the next run from last_execution and the frequency. If the run is due, it enqueues the job.
  5. The job ID is scheduled_job||<Scheduled Job Type name>. A job that is still queued or running is not queued again.
  6. The worker runs the method, commits, and writes a Scheduled Job Log row (Start, Complete or Failed).

The scheduler only queues jobs. If no worker runs, no scheduled job runs.

docs.title: Declare scheduled events
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
scheduler_events = {
    "all": [
        "sample_app.tasks.sync_stock",
    ],
    "hourly": [
        "sample_app.tasks.send_reminders",
    ],
    "daily": [
        "sample_app.tasks.close_old_orders",
    ],
    "daily_long": [
        "sample_app.tasks.rebuild_rates",
    ],
    "weekly": [],
    "monthly": [],
    "cron": {
        "*/15 * * * *": ["sample_app.tasks.poll_service"],
        "30 2 * * 1-5": ["sample_app.tasks.weekday_report"],
    },
}

# sample_app/tasks.py
import frappe


def close_old_orders():
    for name in frappe.get_all("Sample Order", {"status": "Open", "docstatus": 0}, pluck="name"):
        frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name).add_comment("Comment", "Checked by scheduler")

The method takes no arguments. It runs as the user Administrator, the user that the scheduler process uses when it enqueues. Run bench migrate after you change scheduler_events.

docs.title: Event keys
docs.text:
The key in scheduler_events sets the frequency of the Scheduled Job Type. Frappe converts daily_long to Daily Long.

Key Frequency Runs Queue all All Each scheduler_interval seconds (default 240, so each 4 minutes) default hourly Hourly At minute 0 of each hour default hourly_long Hourly Long At minute 0 of each hour long hourly_maintenance Hourly Maintenance Each hour, at a minute offset that depends on the site long daily Daily At 00:00 default daily_long Daily Long At 00:00 long daily_maintenance Daily Maintenance Each day, at a minute offset that depends on the site long weekly Weekly Sunday 00:00 default weekly_long Weekly Long Sunday 00:00 long monthly Monthly 1st day of the month, 00:00 default monthly_long Monthly Long 1st day of the month, 00:00 long yearly, annual Yearly, Annual 1 January, 00:00 default cron Cron The cron expression (dict key) default

Times are in the system time zone of the site. The maintenance offset (0 to 59 minutes) comes from a hash of the site name. It spreads the load when many sites share one bench. Use the _maintenance keys for work that must run about once an hour or day but not at an exact time.

Cron expressions use the croniter syntax. An invalid expression fails validation on save with "Bad Cron Expression".

docs.title: Scheduled Job Type
docs.text:
Open the list at /desk/scheduled-job-type. Fields:

Field Description method Dotted path of the function. frequency See the table above. cron_format Cron expression. Required for Cron. stopped Check to stop this job. Migrate keeps this value. create_log Write a Scheduled Job Log for each run. Always on for frequencies other than All and Cron. last_execution Time of the last run. The next run is computed from it. server_script Set for jobs that come from a Server Script of type Scheduler Event. scheduler_event Link to a Scheduler Event record. Migrate does not delete jobs that have it.

Actions in the form (System Manager only): Execute queues the job now (execute_event). Skip Next Execution moves last_execution to the next run time (skip_next_execution).

Run a job now from the CLI. This runs it in the current process, not in a worker:

bench --site frappe.localhost trigger-scheduler-event sample_app.tasks.close_old_orders

docs.title: Enable and disable
docs.text:
The scheduler is inactive for a site when one of these is true:

  • maintenance_mode is set in site config.
  • pause_scheduler is set in site config.
  • disable_scheduler is set in site config.
  • System Settings > Enable Scheduler (enable_scheduler) is off.
Command Effect bench --site <site> enable-scheduler Sets enable_scheduler = 1 in System Settings. bench --site <site> disable-scheduler Sets enable_scheduler = 0. bench --site <site> scheduler enable\|disable Same as the two commands above. bench --site <site> scheduler pause\|resume Sets or clears pause_scheduler in site_config.json. bench --site <site> scheduler status [-f json] Prints enabled or disabled. bench --site <site> set-maintenance-mode on\|off Sets maintenance_mode. Scheduled jobs do not run in maintenance mode. bench schedule Starts the scheduler process for all sites of the bench. bench doctor Shows scheduler status per site and workers online.

The whitelisted method frappe.utils.scheduler.activate_scheduler (Administrator only) enables the scheduler and clears pause_scheduler. It fails in maintenance mode.

Note

On Frappe Cloud, a site with no user activity for dormant_days (System Settings) runs scheduled jobs only once each 24 hours. This check is off in developer mode and on other hosts.

docs.title: Configuration keys
docs.text: Key File Default Description scheduler_tick_interval common_site_config.json 240 Seconds between scheduler checks. scheduler_interval site or common 240 Interval of all events, in seconds. Converted to whole minutes. pause_scheduler site unset Pause scheduling for the site. disable_scheduler site unset Disable scheduling for the site. maintenance_mode site unset Stops the scheduler and blocks writes.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A job that is still running when its next run is due is skipped, not queued twice.
  • Long jobs on default hold up short ones. Use a _long key. Cron jobs always run on default in v16. To run a long cron job, enqueue the work on long from the cron method.
  • trigger-scheduler-event runs in your shell. Errors show there, not in a worker log.

docs.title: Permissions and Security
docs.text:
Control access with permissions, authenticate clients and write secure code.

Page What it covers Permissions How the permission engine decides access from role permissions, permission levels, user permissions, sharing and app hooks, and how to check permissions in code. Authentication Authenticate HTTP requests with a session cookie, API key and secret, or an OAuth 2 bearer token, and how CSRF, two-factor login, guests and auth hooks work. Security Write secure Frappe app code - permission checks in whitelisted methods, safe SQL, escaping, private files, rate limits, CSRF, secrets and the risks of ignore_permissions.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Each request to a Frappe site runs as one user. frappe.session.user is that user, or Guest if the request is not authenticated. Frappe sets the user from one of these, in frappe/auth.py:

Method Header or cookie Use it for Session sid cookie Browsers, the desk and portal pages API key and secret Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret> Server-to-server scripts and integrations OAuth 2 Authorization: Bearer <access_token> Third-party apps that act for a user Auth hooks anything Custom schemes in your app

All requests on this page were sent with curl to http://frappe.localhost:8006.

docs.title: Session login
docs.text:
curl -s -c cookies.txt -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"usr": "user1@example.com", "pwd": "Sample-Pass-123!"}'

{"message": "Logged In", "home_page": "desk", "full_name": "User 1"}

The response sets the sid cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) and the cookies system_user, full_name, user_id and user_lang. Send the cookie with later requests:

curl -s -b cookies.txt "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

usr is the email. It can also be the user name or the mobile number when System Settings allow_login_using_user_name or allow_login_using_mobile_number is set. Log out with POST /api/method/logout.

Failed logins return HTTP 401 and are written to the Activity Log. Repeated failures lock the user and the IP for a time (LoginAttemptTracker in frappe/auth.py). The login also checks the IP allowlist of the user (restrict_ip) and the login hours (login_after, login_before).

The login runs the before_login and on_login hooks. Logout runs on_logout. Each handler gets login_manager. See Hooks.

docs.title: CSRF
docs.text:
For a cookie session, POST, PUT, DELETE and PATCH requests must send the CSRF token of the session in the X-Frappe-CSRF-Token header (or as csrf_token in the form). Otherwise the request fails with frappe.CSRFTokenError (HTTP 400):

{"exception": "frappe.exceptions.CSRFTokenError: Invalid Request", "exc_type": "CSRFTokenError"}
  • The desk gets the token in frappe.csrf_token and frappe.call sends it for you.
  • A session gets a token the first time it is needed (frappe.sessions.get_csrf_token). A session that has no token yet is not checked.
  • Requests with token or bearer authentication have no session token, so the check does not apply.
  • Requests from an origin or referrer in the site config key allowed_referrers skip the check.
  • The site config key ignore_csrf turns the check off.

docs.title: Generate keys
docs.text:
A System Manager generates the keys for a user:

  1. Open the User in the desk.
  2. Open the API Access section.
  3. Click Generate Keys.
  4. Copy the API Secret from the dialog. It is shown only once.

From code or the API, call frappe.core.doctype.user.user.generate_keys. It requires the System Manager role and POST:

curl -s -b admin_cookies.txt -X POST \
  "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.core.doctype.user.user.generate_keys" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"user": "user1@example.com"}'

{"message": {"api_key": "1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8", "api_secret": "9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2"}}

The API key is created once and does not change. Each call makes a new secret and the old secret stops working. The secret is stored encrypted in the api_secret Password field of the User.

docs.title: Use the keys
docs.text:
curl -s "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" \
  -H "Authorization: token 1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8:9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

HTTP Basic with base64(api_key:api_secret) also works:

curl -s "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" \
  -H "Authorization: Basic $(printf '1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8:9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2' | base64)"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

A wrong key or secret returns HTTP 401 with "exc_type": "AuthenticationError". The failure is not written to the Activity Log.

  • The request runs with the roles and permissions of that user. There is no separate scope.
  • The user must be enabled.
  • The restrict_ip allowlist of the user also applies.
  • No session is created. The response sets the sid cookie to Guest.
  • Two-factor authentication does not apply to token requests.

The header Frappe-Authorization-Source: <DocType> makes Frappe look up the key in another DocType instead of User. That DocType needs the fields api_key, api_secret, enabled and user. The request then runs as the value of user.

docs.title: OAuth 2
docs.text:
Frappe is an OAuth 2 and OpenID Connect provider. A third-party app gets an access token for a user and sends it as a bearer token. Set up the provider and clients in the desk. See Integrations.

Endpoint Path Authorization /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.authorize Token /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token Revocation /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.revoke_token Introspection /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.introspect_token User info (OpenID) /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.openid_profile

The paths are in ENDPOINTS in frappe/integrations/oauth2.py.

docs.title: Authorization code flow
docs.text:
The example uses an OAuth Client with client_id <client_id>, scopes all openid, redirect URI http://localhost:9999/callback, grant type Authorization Code, response type Code and Token Endpoint Auth Method Client Secret Post.

Warning

In v16, the client authentication method Client Secret Basic (the default) does not work. Frappe reads the Authorization: Basic header of the token request as an API key and secret, and returns HTTP 401 with AuthenticationError. Set the OAuth Client to Client Secret Post, and send client_id and client_secret in the form body.

  1. Send the user to the authorization endpoint. A guest is redirected to /login first.

    curl -s -i -b user_cookies.txt -G "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.authorize" \
  --data-urlencode client_id=<client_id> --data-urlencode response_type=code \
  --data-urlencode scope=all --data-urlencode redirect_uri=http://localhost:9999/callback \
  --data-urlencode state=xyz

    HTTP/1.1 302 FOUND
Location: http://localhost:9999/callback?code=<authorization_code>&state=xyz

    The user sees a Confirm Access page first, unless the client has Skip Authorization set.

  2. Exchange the code for tokens. Send client_id and client_secret in the body.

    curl -s -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token" \
  -d client_id=<client_id> -d client_secret=<client_secret> \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code -d code=<authorization_code> \
  -d redirect_uri=http://localhost:9999/callback

    {"access_token": "<access_token>", "expires_in": 3600, "token_type": "Bearer",
 "scope": "all", "refresh_token": "<refresh_token>"}

  3. Call the API with the access token.

    curl -s "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

  4. When the token expires, get a new one with the refresh token. In v16 the old access token keeps working until it expires or you revoke it.

    curl -s -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token" \
  -d client_id=<client_id> -d client_secret=<client_secret> -d grant_type=refresh_token -d refresh_token=<refresh_token>

    {"access_token": "<new_access_token>", "expires_in": 3600, "token_type": "Bearer",
 "scope": "all", "refresh_token": "<new_refresh_token>"}

  5. To end access, revoke the token. The endpoint always returns HTTP 200 with {}.

    curl -s -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8006/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.revoke_token" \
  -d client_id=<client_id> -d client_secret=<client_secret> -d token=<new_access_token>

Tokens are stored as OAuth Bearer Token documents. The access token is the document name, in plain text. An unknown, expired or revoked token, or a token of a disabled user, returns HTTP 401 with frappe.AuthenticationError. The request runs with the roles of the user who approved the token.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
When 2FA applies to a user (System Settings enable_two_factor_auth and a role with Two Factor Authentication set), POST /api/method/login does not log in at once:

  1. The first login request checks the password. The response has tmp_id and a verification object with the method (OTP App, Email or SMS). The user is still Guest.
  2. Send the code: POST /api/method/login with tmp_id and otp. On success the session is created.

The tmp_id expires after 300 seconds for SMS and Email, and after 180 seconds for an OTP App that is set up. The logic is in frappe/twofactor.py.

docs.title: Guests
docs.text:
A request without credentials runs as Guest. The only role of Guest is Guest.

  • A guest can call only methods with @frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True). Other methods return HTTP 403 with "Function ... is not whitelisted".
  • A guest can read documents only through permissions given to the Guest role.
  • Guest string arguments are sanitized for HTML unless the method sets xss_safe=True.

See Whitelisted methods.

docs.title: Custom authentication
docs.text:
The auth_hooks hook lists functions that run on every request after the built-in checks. A function can call frappe.set_user(user) to authenticate the request.

# sample_app/hooks.py
auth_hooks = ["sample_app.auth.validate_sample_header"]

# sample_app/auth.py
import frappe


def validate_sample_header():
    token = frappe.get_request_header("X-Sample-Token")
    if not token:
        return
    user = frappe.db.get_value("Sample Device", {"token": token, "enabled": 1}, "user")
    if user:
        frappe.set_user(user)

If a request has an Authorization header with two parts and no method sets a user, Frappe raises frappe.AuthenticationError (HTTP 401).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• An API secret gives full access as that user. Create a separate user with only the roles the integration needs.
  • generate_keys replaces the secret. Integrations that use the old secret stop working.
  • Do not send API keys in URLs. Use the Authorization header.
  • A cookie session that calls POST from a script must send X-Frappe-CSRF-Token.
  • OAuth clients must use Client Secret Post in v16.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The permission engine decides if a user can do an action on a DocType or on one document. Use this page when you write server code that reads or changes data for a user, or when your app must add its own access rules. To set up roles and rules in the desk, see Role permissions and User Permissions.

docs.title: How a decision is made
docs.text:
frappe.has_permission (in frappe/__init__.py) calls frappe.permissions.has_permission. The engine evaluates these layers in order:

  1. Administrator gets every permission. No other check runs.
  2. If the DocType is a child table, the check runs on the parent DocType. Pass parent_doctype when you do not pass a document.
  3. Role permissions. The engine collects the DocPerm rows (or Custom DocPerm rows, if the DocType has any) at permission level 0 for the roles of the user. A right is granted if any row grants it.
  4. If you pass a document, the engine also applies:
    1. has_permission hooks. They can only deny.
    2. "If Owner" rules. Some rights apply only when doc.owner is the user.
    3. User Permissions on the document itself and on its Link fields.
  5. If access is still denied, the engine checks document sharing (DocShare). Only the rights read, write, share, submit, email, print and custom permission types can be shared.
  6. select is implied by read.

Without a document, the result answers "can the user do this on at least one document of this DocType". With a document, it answers for that document only.

docs.title: Rights
docs.text:
The standard rights are in frappe.permissions.std_rights:

select, read, write, create, delete, submit, cancel, amend, print, email, report, import, export, share.

A DocType can add custom rights with the Permission Type DocType. frappe.permissions.get_rights(doctype) returns the standard and the custom rights.

submit is always false on a DocType that is not submittable. import is always false when allow_import is off.

docs.title: Automatic roles
docs.text:
frappe.get_roles(user) adds roles based on the user type. You do not assign them:

Role Who has it Guest Everybody, including users who are not logged in All Every logged-in user, including website users Desk User System users (desk users) Administrator The Administrator user 
frappe.get_roles("user1@example.com")
# ['Sample Role', 'All', 'Guest', 'Desk User']

docs.title: frappe.has_permission
docs.text:
frappe.has_permission(
    doctype=None, ptype="read", doc=None, user=None, throw=False,
    *, parent_doctype=None, debug=False, ignore_share_permissions=False,
)
Name Type Default Description doctype str None DocType to check. Optional if you pass doc. ptype str "read" Right to check. doc Document or str None Document or document name. Enables document-level checks. user str current user User to check for. throw bool False Raise frappe.PermissionError instead of returning False. parent_doctype str None Required for a child DocType when you do not pass doc. debug bool False Collect the reason for each step in frappe.local.permission_debug_log. ignore_share_permissions bool False Do not grant access through sharing.

Output on the site, as user1@example.com (role Sample Role, which has read, write, create and delete on Sample Item and no rule on Sample Order):

frappe.set_user("user1@example.com")
frappe.has_permission("Sample Item", "read")                  # True
frappe.has_permission("Sample Item", "write", doc="Laptop")   # True
frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "read")                 # False
frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "read", throw=True)     # raises frappe.PermissionError

When throw=True and access is denied for the current user, the engine also shows the reason with frappe.msgprint.

docs.title: Document methods
docs.text:
Method Description doc.has_permission(permtype="read", *, debug=False, user=None) Returns bool. Returns True if doc.flags.ignore_permissions is set. doc.check_permission(permtype="read") Raises frappe.PermissionError if not permitted. frappe.get_doc(doctype, name, check_permission="read") Loads the document and runs check_permission. True means "read".

doc.insert(), doc.save(), doc.submit(), doc.cancel() and frappe.delete_doc() check the matching right. Pass ignore_permissions=True, or set doc.flags.ignore_permissions = True, to skip the check. See Controllers.

docs.title: frappe.only_for
docs.text:
frappe.only_for(roles, message=False) raises frappe.PermissionError if the current user has none of the roles. Administrator always passes. Set message=True to show a "This action is only allowed for ..." message.

frappe.only_for("System Manager")
frappe.only_for(["System Manager", "Sample Role"], message=True)

docs.title: Permission levels
docs.text:
Each field has a permlevel (default 0). A role can read or write fields at level N only if it has a DocPerm row at level N. Level 0 rights decide access to the document itself. Rights at higher levels only control groups of fields.

  • The REST API removes values of fields the user cannot read (doc.apply_fieldlevel_read_permissions).
  • frappe.get_list leaves out fields the user cannot read, also when you ask for *.
  • frappe.get_list raises frappe.PermissionError if you filter, sort or group by a field the user cannot read.
  • doc.save() resets fields at a level the user has no access to back to their stored values (Document.validate_higher_perm_levels). Administrator and ignore_permissions skip this.

docs.title: Permissions in list queries
docs.text:
frappe.get_list and frappe.qb.get_query(..., ignore_permissions=False) add conditions to the SQL query. The logic is in Engine.add_permission_conditions in frappe/database/query.py:

  1. The user needs select or read on the DocType, or the query raises frappe.PermissionError.
  2. If no role gives read or select, the query returns only documents shared with the user.
  3. If read is "If Owner" only, the query adds owner = <user>.
  4. Otherwise the query adds User Permission conditions for the DocType and its Link fields.
  5. The query adds the conditions from permission_query_conditions hooks and from Server Scripts of type Permission Query.
  6. If any condition from steps 3 to 5 applies, shared documents are added with OR.

frappe.get_all sets ignore_permissions=True. It skips all of the above.

frappe.set_user("user1@example.com")
frappe.get_list("Sample Order")    # raises frappe.PermissionError
frappe.get_all("Sample Order", pluck="name")
# ['SO-00006', 'SO-00005', 'SO-00004', 'SO-00003', 'SO-00002', 'SO-00001']

After frappe.share.add("Sample Order", "SO-00002", "user1@example.com", read=1):

frappe.get_list("Sample Order", pluck="name")                         # ['SO-00002']
frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "read", doc="SO-00002")         # True
frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "write", doc="SO-00002")        # False

docs.title: User Permissions in queries
docs.text:
A User Permission restricts a user to some documents of a DocType. It applies to that DocType and to every Link field that points to it, unless the field has ignore_user_permissions set.

from frappe.permissions import add_user_permission

add_user_permission("Sample Item", "Laptop", "user1@example.com")

frappe.set_user("user1@example.com")
frappe.get_list("Sample Item", pluck="name")                                 # ['Laptop']
frappe.has_permission("Sample Item", "read", doc="Monitor")                  # False
frappe.get_list("Sample Item", pluck="name", ignore_user_permissions=True)   # all items

Helpers in frappe/permissions.py:

Function Description add_user_permission(doctype, name, user, ignore_permissions=False, applicable_for=None, is_default=0, hide_descendants=0) Creates a User Permission. Raises frappe.DoesNotExistError if the document does not exist. remove_user_permission(doctype, name, user, ignore_permissions=False) Deletes it. clear_user_permissions_for_doctype(doctype, user=None) Deletes all User Permissions for a DocType. get_user_permissions(user) Returns the User Permissions of a user, grouped by DocType.

docs.title: has_permission hook
docs.text:
Use the has_permission hook to deny access to single documents with Python logic. The hook runs only for document-level checks.

# sample_app/hooks.py
has_permission = {
    "Sample Order": "sample_app.permissions.sample_order_has_permission",
}

# sample_app/permissions.py
def sample_order_has_permission(doc, ptype=None, user=None, debug=False):
    if ptype == "write" and doc.status == "Completed":
        return False
    return True

Rules:

  • The hook can only deny. It cannot grant a right that role permissions do not give.
  • Return True to allow. Every falsy value denies, including None. A function that ends without return denies access.
  • Handlers for "*" run for every DocType. Handlers run in reverse order, and the first denial stops the check.
  • The hook is called with frappe.call, so it receives only the arguments it declares from doc, ptype, user and debug.

Warning

The hook does not run for list queries. Add a matching permission_query_conditions hook, or frappe.get_list will show documents that has_permission denies.

docs.title: permission_query_conditions hook
docs.text:
Use permission_query_conditions to filter list queries. The function returns a SQL condition string, or a query builder criterion. An empty value adds no condition.

# sample_app/hooks.py
permission_query_conditions = {
    "Sample Order": "sample_app.permissions.sample_order_query",
}

# sample_app/permissions.py
import frappe


def sample_order_query(user, doctype=None):
    if user == "Administrator" or "System Manager" in frappe.get_roles(user):
        return ""
    return f"`tabSample Order`.`owner_user` = {frappe.db.escape(user)}"

Rules:

  • The function receives user and the keyword argument doctype.
  • The engine wraps a string in parentheses and joins all conditions with AND.
  • The hook also runs for Administrator. Return an empty string for users that must see everything.
  • Escape every value with frappe.db.escape. The string goes into the SQL as it is.

docs.title: Custom permission types
docs.text: The Permission Type DocType adds a right to one DocType. Check it like a standard right: frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "approve", doc=doc). Custom rights can also be shared.

docs.title: Ignore permissions safely
docs.text:
Code Effect frappe.get_all(...) No permission conditions. frappe.get_list(..., ignore_permissions=True) Same as frappe.get_all. doc.insert(ignore_permissions=True), doc.save(ignore_permissions=True) Skips the right check for this call. doc.flags.ignore_permissions = True Skips the right check for all later actions on this object. frappe.db.* methods Never check permissions.

Arguments that come from an HTTP request never reach your function as ignore_permissions or flags. frappe.get_newargs removes them before the call. Make sure you do not read them from frappe.form_dict.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• frappe.get_all and frappe.db.* return data the user may not see. In a whitelisted method, use frappe.get_list, or check frappe.has_permission(..., throw=True) first.
  • A has_permission hook that returns None denies access.
  • A permission_query_conditions hook without an Administrator check also filters the list for Administrator.
  • has_permission without doc returns True if the user can access at least one document. It does not apply User Permissions or hooks.
  • Sharing overrides User Permissions and query hooks in list queries.
