docs.title: Customization
docs.text:
Change forms and fields without code, and define document workflows.

Page What it covers Customize Form Change the fields, layout and properties of a standard DocType from the desk with Customize Form, Custom Field and Property Setter. Workflow Move documents through approval states with Workflow, Workflow State, transitions and Workflow Action.

docs.title: Customize Form
docs.text: Use Customize Form to change a standard DocType on one site without editing the app code. You can add fields, hide or reorder fields, change labels and other field properties, and change DocType settings such as the title field or the sort order. Your changes survive app updates, because Frappe stores them in two separate DocTypes: Custom Field and Property Setter.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Record DocType What it stores Name format New field Custom Field A field that you add to a DocType. Frappe adds a column to the database table. <DocType>-<fieldname>, for example ToDo-custom_sample_ref Changed property Property Setter One changed property of a DocType, a field, a link, an action or a state. <DocType>-<field or row or "main">-<property>, for example ToDo-priority-reqd
  • When you add a field and do not give a fieldname, Frappe makes one from the label and adds the prefix custom_. A label "Sample Ref" gives custom_sample_ref.
  • Property Setter doctype_or_field ("Applied On") is one of DocField, DocType, DocType Link, DocType Action or DocType State.
  • Frappe merges Custom Fields and Property Setters into the DocType meta when it loads the meta (frappe.get_meta).
  • Only users with the System Manager role can use Customize Form.

docs.title: What you cannot customize
docs.text:
Customize Form rejects these DocTypes:

  • Core DocTypes in frappe.model.core_doctypes_list, for example DocType, User, Role, Report, Print Format, Custom Field and Property Setter. The error is "Core DocTypes cannot be customized."
  • Single DocTypes. The error is "Single DocTypes cannot be customized."
  • Custom DocTypes (DocTypes with custom set, such as Sample Item). For these, the desk opens the DocType form instead, where you edit the DocType directly.

docs.title: Open Customize Form
docs.text:
1. Open the list or a form of the DocType, for example ToDo.
  2. Open the menu (the ... button).
  3. Select Customize. In the list view the shortcut is Ctrl+Y.

You can also go to /desk/customize-form and select the DocType in Enter Form Type (doc_type).

The form has two tabs:

  • Form shows the form builder. Drag fields, sections, columns and tabs to change the layout. Click a field to edit its properties in the right panel. Click Add field to add a Custom Field.
  • Details shows the DocType properties, the Fields table, and the Document Actions, Document Links and Document States tables.

Click Update to save. Frappe then creates or updates the Custom Fields and Property Setters, updates the database table if a column changed, and clears the cache of the DocType.

docs.title: Add a field
docs.text:
1. Open Customize Form for ToDo.
  2. In the Form tab, click Add field in the column where you want the field.
  3. Select the field type and enter the label, for example "Sample Ref".
  4. Set other properties in the right panel, for example Mandatory or In List View.
  5. Click Update.

To delete a Custom Field, remove it in the form builder and click Update. You cannot delete a standard field. Hide it instead.

docs.title: Change a standard field
docs.text:
You can change properties of standard fields, for example the label, Hidden, Mandatory, Read Only, In List View, Default, Depends On and the permission level. Each changed property becomes one Property Setter.

Frappe limits field type changes. You can change the type only inside a group of compatible types (ALLOWED_FIELDTYPE_CHANGE in frappe/custom/doctype/customize_form/customize_form.py). If the new type is shorter and saved values are too long, Frappe shows "Data Too Long" and lists the documents.

docs.title: DocType properties
docs.text:
These properties are in the Details tab. The list is not complete.

Label Fieldname Description Change Label (via Custom Translation) label Shows another name for the DocType. Frappe saves it as a Translation record. Search Fields search_fields Fields that Link field search also looks in. Title Field title_field Field shown as the document title. Show Title in Link Fields show_title_field_in_link Shows the title, not the name, in Link fields. Image Field image_field Field used as the document image. Quick Entry quick_entry Opens a small dialog for new documents. Track Changes track_changes Saves a Version record for each change. Track Views track_views Logs who opened a document. Allow Import (via Data Import Tool) allow_import Allows Data Import for this DocType. Allow Auto Repeat allow_auto_repeat Adds an auto_repeat Custom Field so documents can repeat. Max Attachments max_attachments Maximum number of attachments per document. Hide Sidebar, Menu, and Comments hide_toolbar Hides the form sidebar, menu and comments. Naming Rule / Auto Name naming_rule, autoname How new documents get a name. Default Print Format default_print_format Print format used by default. Default View default_view View that opens from the sidebar, for example List or Report. Sort Field / Sort Order sort_field, sort_order Default sort of the list view. Allow document creation via Email email_append_to Creates documents from incoming email.

docs.title: Actions menu
docs.text:
The Actions button has these items:

Item What it does Go to {DocType} List Opens the list view. Not shown for child tables. Set Permissions Opens the Role Permissions Manager for this DocType. Reload Loads the current customizations again. Reset Layout Deletes the Property Setters for field_order and insert_after. Reset All Customizations Deletes all Property Setters and Custom Fields of the DocType that are not system generated. Property Setters for naming_series and options stay. Trim Table Removes database columns that no field uses anymore. You cannot undo this. Export Customizations Shown only in developer mode. See below.

To customize a child table, use Customize Child Table and select the table.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
Do not ask users to repeat customizations on each site. Ship them with your app.

Export from the desk. In developer mode, click Actions > Export Customizations. Select a module. Frappe writes the Custom Fields, Property Setters and links to <module>/custom/<doctype>.json in your app, and does the same for each child table. If Sync on Migrate is set, bench migrate applies the file on each site. If Export Custom Permissions is set, the file also holds the Custom DocPerm rules, and migrate force-syncs them.

Create them in code. Use create_custom_fields in an install hook or a patch. It creates the fields that do not exist and updates the ones that do.

# sample_app/setup.py
from frappe.custom.doctype.custom_field.custom_field import create_custom_fields
from frappe.custom.doctype.property_setter.property_setter import make_property_setter


def after_install():
    create_custom_fields(
        {
            "ToDo": [
                {
                    "fieldname": "sample_ref",
                    "label": "Sample Ref",
                    "fieldtype": "Data",
                    "insert_after": "description",
                }
            ]
        }
    )
    make_property_setter("ToDo", "priority", "reqd", 1, "Check")
  • create_custom_fields(custom_fields, ignore_validate=False, update=True) creates the records as Administrator, clears the cache and updates the table.
  • make_property_setter(doctype, fieldname, property, value, property_type, for_doctype=False, ...) ignores permissions. Set for_doctype=True for a DocType property.
  • You can also export Custom Field and Property Setter records with the fixtures hook. See Fixtures and Patches and Extending Apps.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A field type change that makes a column smaller can fail if saved values are too long.
  • Many fields can hit the database row size limit. Frappe then shows "Database Table Row Size Limit".
  • Reset All Customizations also removes Custom Fields that other users added. Export them first if you need them.
  • Customizations that an app ships with is_system_generated set stay after a reset.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: A Workflow controls how a document moves from one state to the next, and which role can move it. Use it when a document needs review or approval before it is submitted, for example "Pending" to "Approved". When a workflow applies to a document, the form shows an Actions menu instead of the standard Submit and Cancel buttons.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Term DocType Meaning Workflow Workflow The rule set for one DocType: states and transitions. State Workflow State A named stage, for example "Pending". It has an optional icon and button style. Action Workflow Action Master A named step a user clicks, for example "Approve". Transition Workflow Transition (child) "From state X, role R can do action A to go to state Y." Workflow Action Workflow Action A to-do record that Frappe creates for users who can act on a document in its current state.

The current state of each document is stored in the field named in Workflow State Field (default workflow_state). If the DocType has no such field, Frappe adds a hidden Custom Field of type Link to Workflow State when you save the workflow.

docs.title: Create a workflow
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/workflow/new.
  2. Enter a Workflow Name and select the Document Type.
  3. In Document States, add one row for each state.
  4. In Transitions, add one row for each allowed move between states.
  5. Select Is Active.
  6. Save.

You can also edit states and transitions on a canvas in the Workflow Builder (/desk/workflow-builder).

docs.title: Document States
docs.text: Field Description State (state) A Workflow State record. Doc Status (doc_status) 0 Draft, 1 Submitted, 2 Cancelled. A non-submittable DocType can only use 0. Only Allow Edit For (allow_edit) The role that can edit the document in this state. Update Field / Update Value Set a field of the document when it enters this state. Evaluate as Expression Treat Update Value as a Python expression, for example doc.total * 2. Is Optional State Do not create Workflow Action records for this state. Send Email On State (send_email) Default on. Send the action email when the document enters this state (needs Send Email Alert on the workflow). Next Action Email Template An Email Template for that email. Message A message to show for this state. Don't Override Status Do not show the workflow state as the list view status.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
Field Description State / Next State The state before and after the action. Action A Workflow Action Master record. Allowed (allowed) The role that can do this action. Allow Self Approval Default on. When off, the document owner cannot do this action. Administrator is always allowed. Send Email To Creator Default off. When off, the document owner gets no action email for this transition. Condition Optional Python expression. The action shows only when it is true. Transition Tasks Optional Workflow Transition Tasks record: Server Scripts, Webhooks or app tasks that run with the transition.

Transition conditions get doc (the document as a dict) and a limited frappe object: frappe.db.get_value, frappe.db.get_list, frappe.session, and frappe.utils.now_datetime, add_to_date, get_datetime, now.

doc.total > 0 and doc.customer_name != "Customer A"

Frappe checks these rules when it saves a workflow:

  • A non-submittable DocType can only have states with Doc Status 0.
  • A transition cannot start from a Cancelled state.
  • A transition cannot go from Submitted (1) back to Draft (0).
  • A transition cannot go from Draft (0) to Cancelled (2).

docs.title: Workflow options
docs.text:
Field Default Description Is Active 0 Only the active workflow applies. Don't Override Status 0 Keep the document status in list view instead of the workflow state. Send Email Alert 0 Email the users who can do the next action. Enable Action Confirmation 0 Ask the user to confirm before an action runs.

A DocType has one active workflow. When you save a workflow with Is Active selected, Frappe deactivates all other workflows of that DocType.

When you save a workflow, Frappe sets the state field of existing documents that have no state yet. It uses the first state row for each docstatus.

docs.title: Use a workflow on a document
docs.text:
1. Open the document.
  2. Click Actions.
  3. Select an action.

The menu shows only the transitions from the current state that your roles allow and whose condition is true. After the action, Frappe saves, submits or cancels the document to match the docstatus of the next state. It also adds a "Workflow" comment to the timeline.

To apply an action to many documents, select them in the list view and use the Actions menu. Fewer than 20 documents run at once. From 20 to 500 documents run in a background job. More than 500 documents are rejected.

docs.title: Workflow Action records
docs.text: After each save, cancel or update after submit, Frappe creates Workflow Action records with status Open for the roles that can do the next transition. The user sees them in the Workflow Action list. When Send Email Alert is on, Frappe also emails these users. The email has links to do the action without logging in to desk. When a user does the action, the records change to Completed.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A user can only change the state with a valid transition. A direct edit of the state field fails with "Workflow State transition not allowed".
  • Data Import cannot insert documents in a state other than the first state.
  • If the state stored on a document is not in the workflow, save fails. Update the workflow or the document.
  • A cancelled state blocks the standard Cancel button. Use a transition to the cancelled state.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Server API in frappe/model/workflow.py: apply_workflow(doc, action), get_transitions(doc, workflow=None, raise_exception=False), bulk_workflow_approval(docnames, doctype, action), get_workflow_name(doctype).
  • Add your own transition tasks with the workflow_methods hook. Each entry is a dict with name and method. The method gets the document.
# sample_app/hooks.py
workflow_methods = [
    {"name": "Notify Warehouse", "method": "sample_app.tasks.notify_warehouse"},
]

# sample_app/tasks.py
def notify_warehouse(doc):
    ...
  • Synchronous tasks run in the same transaction as the transition. Tasks marked Asynchronous run in a background job after commit.
  • process_workflow_actions runs from doc_events for * (on_update, on_cancel, on_trash, on_update_after_submit) in frappe/hooks.py.

Version

Workflow conditions and priority, which let more than one workflow be active on a DocType, are not in v16.

docs.title: Data, Reports and Printing
docs.text:
Import and export data, run reports, build dashboards and print documents.

Page What it covers Data Import and Export Insert or update many records from CSV, Excel or Google Sheets with Data Import, fix invalid values, read the import log, and export records with Data Export. Reports Build and save Report Builder reports, run Query and Script Reports, use prepared reports for slow reports, and export results to Excel or CSV. Dashboards Show counts and charts with Number Card and Dashboard Chart, group them in a Dashboard, and add them to workspaces. Printing Print documents, download PDFs, and design Print Formats with the Print Format Editor, Jinja HTML or raw commands, plus Letter Head and Print Settings.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text: A Number Card shows one number, such as the count of open orders. A Dashboard Chart shows data over time or by group. A Dashboard puts cards and charts on one page. You can also add cards and charts to a workspace. Use them to give users a quick view of the data they work with.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: DocType Route What it is Number Card /desk/number-card One number from a DocType, a report or a whitelisted method. Dashboard Chart /desk/dashboard-chart A chart from a DocType, a report or a custom source. Dashboard /desk/dashboard A named set of charts and cards. Shown at /desk/dashboard-view/<name>. Dashboard Chart Source /desk/dashboard-chart-source Code in an app that gives data to a Custom chart. Dashboard Settings none Per-user chart setup (chart_config), such as saved chart filters.

docs.title: Make a Number Card
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/number-card/new.
  2. Enter a Label. The label is also the name of the card.
  3. Set Type to Document Type.
  4. Select the Document Type, for example Sample Order.
  5. Select the Function: Count, Sum, Average, Minimum or Maximum.
  6. If the function is not Count, select the number field in Aggregate Function Based On.
  7. Click the filters table and set filters, for example status = Open.
  8. Save.
  9. Click Add Card to Dashboard to put it on a Dashboard.
Field Default Description type Document Type, Report or Custom. function For Document Type. parent_document_type Needed when the Document Type is a child table. report_name, report_field, report_function For Report: the report, the number column, and Sum, Average, Minimum or Maximum. method For Custom: dotted path of a whitelisted method. filters_json Fixed filters. dynamic_filters_json Filters with JavaScript expressions, for example frappe.datetime.get_today(). show_percentage_stats 1 Shows the change from the previous period. stats_time_interval Daily Period for the change: Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Yearly. is_public 0 Makes the card available to all users. color, background_color Card colors. show_full_number 0 Shows the full number instead of a short form.

docs.title: Make a Dashboard Chart
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/dashboard-chart/new.
  2. Enter Chart Name.
  3. Select the Chart Type.
  4. Select the Document Type and set the fields for that chart type.
  5. Select the display Type: Line, Bar, Percentage, Pie, Donut or Heatmap.
  6. Set filters in the filters table.
  7. Save.
  8. Click Add Chart to Dashboard to put it on a Dashboard.
Chart Type Fields to set Result Count Time Series Based On (a date field), Timespan, Time Interval Number of records per period. Sum / Average Same as Count, plus Value Based On Sum or average of a number field per period. Group By Group By Based On, Group By Type (Count, Sum, Average), Number of Groups One value per group, for example per status. Report Report Name, X Field, Y Axis, or Use Report Chart Chart from the data of a report. Custom Chart Source Data from a Dashboard Chart Source in an app.

Timespan can be Last Year, Last Quarter, Last Month, Last Week or Select Date Range. Time Interval can be Yearly, Quarterly, Monthly, Weekly or Daily. Cancelled documents are never counted.

The chart menu on a dashboard has Refresh, Edit, Reset Chart, Export, and a link to the list or report of the source. Chart data is cached. Refresh gets new data and shows the time in Last synced.

docs.title: Make a Dashboard
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/dashboard/new.
  2. Enter Dashboard Name.
  3. Add charts in the Charts table. Set the Width of each chart to Half or Full.
  4. Add cards in the Cards table.
  5. Save.
  6. Click Show Dashboard.

Is Default makes this the default dashboard. Chart Options takes JSON that applies to all charts on the dashboard.

docs.title: Add cards and charts to a workspace
docs.text:
1. Open the workspace.
  2. Click Edit.
  3. Add a Chart block or a Number Card block.
  4. Select an existing chart or card, or make a new one.
  5. Save the workspace.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
• System Managers see all charts and cards.
  • A user sees a Count, Sum, Average or Group By chart, or a Document Type card, when they can read its DocType. A Report chart or card needs access to the report.
  • The chart list does not show Custom charts to users without System Manager.
  • If a chart has rows in its Roles table, a user with one of those roles can open it.
  • Charts and cards are also limited to the modules the user can see.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• A Custom Number Card calls the whitelisted method in method with filters. Return a number, or a dict with value and the formatting keys such as fieldtype.
  • A Custom chart reads frappe.dashboards.chart_sources["<Source Name>"] from <module>/dashboard_chart_source/<source_name>/<source_name>.js in your app. Set method there to the Python method that returns the chart data.
  • Cards and charts with Is Standard set are exported to the module of the app when you save in developer mode. A standard chart cannot be edited on a site without developer mode.
  • Chart data comes from frappe.desk.doctype.dashboard_chart.dashboard_chart.get and card data from frappe.desk.doctype.number_card.number_card.get_result.
  • Ship charts and cards in a workspace of your app. See Workspaces, Sidebar and Dock.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• The Document Type picker of a Number Card does not offer Single DocTypes.
  • A card with a function other than Count needs Aggregate Function Based On. Save does not check the field type, so pick a number field.
  • Chart data is cached per chart. Use Refresh after a large data change.

docs.title: Data Import and Export
docs.text: Data Import inserts or updates many records from a CSV or Excel file, or from a public Google Sheet. Data Export downloads records as CSV or Excel. Use them to move data in from another system, to change many records at once, or to get a template to fill in.

docs.title: Before you import
docs.text:
• The DocType must allow import (Allow Import in the DocType or Customize Form).
  • You need the import permission on the DocType.
  • Most core DocTypes cannot be imported. User, Role and Print Format can.
  • The scheduler must be active, because the import runs in a background job. In developer mode, the import runs in the request.

docs.title: Import records
docs.text: Go to /desk/data-import/new, or open the list view of the DocType and select Import from the new-record menu. The import has four steps: Config, Preview, Fix issues and Import. Frappe names the record <DocType> Import on <creation time>, for example Sample Item Import on 2026-11-22 05:47:50.493621.

docs.title: 1. Config
docs.text:
1. Select the Document Type.
  2. Select the Import Type.
  3. Optional: click Download Template to get a file with the right columns.
  4. Attach the file in Import File, or enter a URL in Import from Google Sheets.
  5. Click Next.
Import Type Result Insert New Records Each row makes a new document. Update Existing Records Each row updates the document in the ID column. A row with no change fails with "No changes to update". Insert or Update Records Update the document if the ID exists, else insert it. Option Default Description Don't Send Emails (mute_emails) 1 Do not send emails or notifications during the import. Submit After Import 0 Submit each document. Submittable DocTypes only. Custom Delimiters / Delimiter Options 0 / ,;\t| For CSV files with a delimiter other than a comma. Detect CSV type (use_csv_sniffer) 0 Let Frappe find the CSV format.

docs.title: 2. Preview
docs.text:
The preview shows the rows of the file. Each column has a field picker. Change it to match a column to another field, or select Don't Import to skip the column. Save to apply the change. Click Next to go to the next step.

For a tree DocType, the preview shows the tree. You can change the parent of a node or mark it as a group before the import.

docs.title: 3. Fix issues
docs.text:
Frappe checks Link and Select values, dates and mandatory fields. Each value that is not valid gets a row in Mapping warnings:

  • Enter a valid value in Map To. Frappe uses it for every row with that value.
  • For a Link field, select Create New to create the missing record during the import.
  • Or click Skip to leave out every row that has the value.

The import does not start while there are warnings that are not fixed or skipped.

docs.title: 4. Import
docs.text:
Click Import. Frappe shows the progress, and then the result: how many records were inserted, updated, failed or skipped.

  • Frappe commits after each successful row. A failed row does not undo the rows before it.
  • The status of the import becomes Success, Partial Success, Error or Timed Out.
  • If some rows fail, fix the data and start the import again. Rows that were imported before are not imported again.
  • Click Cancel to stop a running import. Frappe asks you to confirm, then stops the job and sets the status to Error.

docs.title: Import log
docs.text:
Each imported or failed row makes a Data Import Log record with the document name, the row numbers, a success flag and the error. On the Import step you can filter the log, and download:

  • Download Failed Rows (on the Failed count): a file with only the rows that failed, to fix and import again.
  • Download Skipped Rows (on the Skipped count): the rows you chose to skip.
  • Export Import Log: the full log.

Deleting a Data Import also deletes its logs.

docs.title: Export records
docs.text:
There are two ways to export records.

From a list view (recommended): select records, then use Actions > Export. Or open the Data Import form and click Download Template. The Export Data dialog has these options:

Option Values File Type Excel or CSV Export Type All Records, Filtered Records, 5 Records or Blank Template Fields The fields of the DocType and its child tables. Use Select Mandatory or Select All.

The exported file has the same format that Data Import reads, so you can edit it and import it with Update Existing Records.

Data Export page: go to /desk/data-export. Select the DocType, the File Type (Excel or CSV), filters and fields, then click Export. Select Export without main header to leave out the header notes and column descriptions.

To export the rows shown in a report, use Export in the menu of the report view. See Reports.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• When you update records, include the ID column. Frappe finds the document by it.
  • In Insert mode, Frappe sets the name from the file only when the DocType uses Prompt naming.
  • A workflow DocType can only import documents in the first workflow state.
  • Child table rows go on the lines below their parent row, with the parent columns empty.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Import from the command line:
bench --site frappe.localhost data-import --file sample-items.csv --doctype "Sample Item" --type Insert

--type is Insert, Update or Upsert. Add --submit-after-import to submit. The path is relative to the sites folder.

  • Import or export JSON records from code with import_doc(path) and export_json(doctype, path, filters=None) in frappe/core/doctype/data_import/data_import.py. bench import-doc <path> uses import_doc.
  • Take over validation and record creation for one DocType with the data_import_providers hook. Map the DocType to a subclass of ImportProvider in frappe/core/doctype/data_import/import_provider.py.
# sample_app/hooks.py
data_import_providers = {"Sample Order": "sample_app.imports.SampleOrderImport"}
  • Rows per batch: data_import_batch_size in site config (default 1000). See Site Config.

docs.title: Printing
docs.text: Every document in the desk can be printed or saved as a PDF. A Print Format controls what the printed page shows. Use the print view to print, download or email a document. Make a Print Format when the standard layout does not fit, for example when an invoice needs a custom header or a narrow receipt layout.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: Name DocType What it is Print view page print The preview at /desk/print/<DocType>/<name>. You pick the format, letter head, style and paper there. Print Format Print Format A layout for one DocType (or one report). Made in the Print Format Editor, in the classic Print Format Builder, or written as Jinja HTML. Standard format none The layout Frappe makes from the form when no Print Format is selected. Letter Head Letter Head A header and footer (image or HTML) added to the top and bottom of a print. Print Style Print Style Site-wide CSS for printed pages. Standard styles: Redesign, Modern, Classic, Striped, Monochrome. Print Settings Print Settings (Single) Site defaults: PDF engine, page size, draft and cancelled printing, raw printing. Print Heading Print Heading A named heading text that a print can show.

docs.title: Print a document
docs.text:
1. Open the document.
  2. Click the print icon in the form sidebar, or press Ctrl+P. The print view opens.
  3. In the sidebar, select a Print Format, Language and Letter Head.
  4. Select a Style, a Font, a Paper Size and an Orientation if you need them.
  5. Click Print to send the page to the browser print dialog.

The toolbar icons do these actions:

Icon Action Shortcut Download Download PDF. Makes the PDF on the server. Ctrl+Shift+P Mail Email. Opens the email composer with the print attached. Ctrl+Shift+E Form Goes back to the form. Print button Print. Opens the browser print dialog. Ctrl+P

The ... menu has Full Page, Refresh, Set as Default Format, Print Settings and Customize. Raw Printing Setting shows when raw printing is on. Select Network Printer shows when Enable Print Server is on in Print Settings.

When Print the PDF (print_generated_pdf) is on in Print Settings, Print prints the PDF from the server instead of the page preview.

Note

Draft documents print with a "Draft" heading when Always add "Draft" Heading for printing draft documents is on in Print Settings. Cancelled documents print only when Allow Print for Cancelled is on.

docs.title: Make a Print Format with the editor
docs.text:
A new Print Format that is not a custom HTML format uses the Print Format Editor. The form sets Print Format Editor (print_format_builder_beta) and PDF Generator chrome for a new format.

  1. Go to /desk/print-format/new.
  2. Enter a name and select the DocType, for example Sample Order.
  3. Save. The editor opens at /desk/print-format-builder-beta/<name>.
  4. Select Start from default to begin with all fields of the DocType, or Start blank.
  5. Drag fields from the left panel onto the page.
  6. Click Save & Apply to make the change live.

To open the editor later, click Edit Format in the Print Format form.

The left panel has four tabs:

Tab Content Fields The fields of the DocType and of its child tables. Layers The tree of sections and fields on the page. Blocks Section, Page Break, Custom HTML (or Typst for a Typst format), Spacer, Divider, Image, Barcode, Custom Table, Text and Linked Field. Library Saved snippets that you can reuse.

The right panel has the sections Typography, Style, Page, Spacing (mm), Page background, Document (PDF renderer, Letter head, Page numbers), Access (roles that may print with this format) and Custom CSS.

The editor keeps your edits as a working draft (draft_data) until you click Save & Apply. The history icon shows saved versions. The record box at the top picks the document used for the preview.

docs.title: PDF renderer
docs.text: Value Label in the editor Notes chrome Chromium Default for editor formats. Renders HTML with headless Chromium. PlutoPrint PlutoPrint (light) Falls back to Chromium for a format it cannot render. Typst Typst (fast) Only for editor formats. Adds a Typst block and removes Custom HTML. WeasyPrint WeasyPrint Shows only when a format already uses it. Marked "Deprecated, removed in version 17".

docs.title: Classic Print Format Builder
docs.text: A format with Print Format Builder (print_format_builder) on and Print Format Editor off opens in the classic builder at /desk/print-format-builder/<name>. The form shows "The classic builder will be removed in version 17." Click Convert to new builder to move the layout to the editor. Restore classic layout brings back the backup of the classic layout.

docs.title: Write a Jinja Print Format
docs.text:
Use a Jinja format when you need full control of the HTML.

  1. Open a new Print Format and select the DocType.
  2. Turn on Custom Format.
  3. Keep Print Format Type as Jinja.
  4. Write the template in HTML.
  5. Save.
<h2>{{ doc.customer_name }}</h2>
<p>{{ _("Order Date") }}: {{ doc.get_formatted("order_date") }}</p>
<table class="table table-bordered">
  {% for row in doc.items %}
  <tr>
    <td>{{ row.item }}</td>
    <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("qty") }}</td>
    <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("rate", doc) }}</td>
  </tr>
  {% endfor %}
</table>
<p class="text-right">{{ _("Total") }}: {{ doc.get_formatted("total") }}</p>

The template gets doc, meta, layout, no_letterhead, letter_head, footer and print_settings, plus the Jinja globals such as frappe and _. Frappe validates the template on save.

A custom format can set PDF Generator to wkhtmltopdf, chrome, PlutoPrint, Typst or WeasyPrint. Empty uses the engine in Print Settings. Paper Size (A4, A5, A3, Letter, Legal, Receipt 80 mm, Receipt 58 mm) shows only for chrome and PlutoPrint.

docs.title: Raw printing
docs.text: For label and receipt printers, turn on Custom Format and Raw Printing, then write printer commands in Raw Commands. Turn on Enable Raw Printing in Print Settings first. The browser sends raw commands to the printer through the QZ Tray client.

docs.title: Print Format for a report
docs.text: Set Print Format For to Report and select the Report. Frappe sets Custom Format for report formats, so you write the HTML yourself.

docs.title: Set the default format
docs.text:
• In the Print Format form, click Set as Default. For a custom DocType this sets default_print_format on the DocType. For other DocTypes it makes a Property Setter.
  • In the print view, use ... > Set as Default Format.

Disabling the default format removes it as the default after you confirm.

docs.title: Letter Head
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/letter-head/new.
  2. Enter Letter Head Name.
  3. Set Letter Head Based On to Image or HTML.
  4. Add the header image or the Header HTML.
  5. Set Footer Based On and add the footer the same way.
  6. Turn on Default Letter Head to use it when no letter head is picked.

Header and footer HTML are Jinja. They get doc when they render.

docs.title: Print Settings
docs.text:
Go to /desk/print-settings.

Field Default Description send_print_as_pdf 1 Attach prints to emails as PDF. repeat_header_footer 1 Repeat the letter head header and footer on each PDF page. print_generated_pdf 0 The Print button prints the PDF from the server instead of the page preview. pdf_generator chrome Default PDF engine: wkhtmltopdf, chrome or PlutoPrint. A format can override it. pdf_page_size A4 Default PDF page size. Custom shows pdf_page_height and pdf_page_width in mm. with_letterhead 1 Print with the default letter head. allow_print_for_draft 1 Allow printing of draft documents. add_draft_heading 1 Add a "Draft" heading to draft prints. allow_print_for_cancelled 0 Allow printing of cancelled documents. allow_page_break_inside_tables 0 Let a table split across pages. enable_print_server 0 Print to a network printer (Network Printer Settings, CUPS server and port 631 by default). enable_raw_printing 0 Allow raw command formats. print_style Redesign Default Print Style. font Default Default print font. font_size In points. Empty uses 9. max_bulk_print_docs 100 Most documents in one bulk PDF export. max_concurrent_bulk_exports 5 Most bulk PDF exports one user can have queued or running at the same time.

Note

The field help says wkhtmltopdf is deprecated and will be removed in version 17. When a format renders with wkhtmltopdf, the print view checks the installed version and warns if it is not the patched-Qt 0.12.x build.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Get the HTML or PDF of a document in Python with frappe.get_print. It uses the PDF engine from the format or Print Settings.
html = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001", print_format="Sample Order Print")
pdf = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001", as_pdf=True)  # bytes, starts with b"%PDF-"
  • Use frappe.attach_print(doctype, name, ...) to get a PDF attachment dict (fname, fcontent) for frappe.sendmail.
  • The download URL is /api/method/frappe.utils.print_format.download_pdf?doctype=...&name=...&format=.... It checks print permission. It has a concurrency limit (frappe.concurrent_limit), not a per-user rate limit.
  • Add Jinja methods and filters for templates with the jinja hook ({"methods": [...], "filters": [...]}).
  • Add a PDF engine with the pdf_generator hook. Frappe registers get_chrome_pdf, get_plutoprint_pdf, get_typst_pdf and get_weasyprint_pdf.
  • Other hooks: get_print_format_template, on_print_pdf, pdf_header_html, pdf_body_html, pdf_footer_html.
  • A Print Format with Standard = Yes is saved in the app and can be changed only in developer mode. See Print Formats.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A standard Print Format cannot be changed on a site. Duplicate it and edit the copy.
  • Edits in the Print Format Editor do not print until you click Save & Apply.
  • An editor format always renders with chrome, PlutoPrint, Typst or WeasyPrint. Other values fall back to chrome.
  • The Access roles hide the format from users without one of the roles.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text: A report shows records as a table, with filters, totals, charts and export. Frappe has four report types. Use Report Builder to save a column and filter setup of one DocType without code. Use a Query Report or a Script Report when you need joins, calculations or data from many DocTypes. Every report is a Report document.

docs.title: Report types
docs.text:
report_type Who makes it Where it runs Notes Report Builder A user with create permission on Report (by default Report Manager, System Manager) Report view of one DocType Columns, filters, sort, group by and totals are saved as JSON in the json field. Query Report Script Manager (non-standard) or a developer /desk/query-report/<name> One SQL SELECT in the query field. Script Report Script Manager (non-standard) or a developer /desk/query-report/<name> Python. In an app: an execute(filters) function. On a site: the Script field. Custom Report Report Manager /desk/query-report/<name> A saved copy of a Query or Script Report with its own columns and filters. reference_report points to the original.

A report is Standard (is_standard = Yes) when it is part of an app. A standard report cannot be changed on a site. Duplicate it, or use Save in the report to make a Custom Report.

A non-standard report can have a Letter Head (letter_head) for its prints. Frappe clears it on save for a standard report.

docs.title: Make a Report Builder report
docs.text:
1. Open the list of the DocType, for example /desk/sample-order.
  2. Switch the view to Report. The URL becomes /desk/sample-order/view/report.
  3. Add filters with Filter, and a group with Add Group.
  4. Click a column header to sort or remove the column. Use ... > Pick Columns to add columns, also from child tables.
  5. Click ... > Save As and enter a name.

The new report opens at /desk/<doctype>/view/report/<report name>. The page title shows Not Saved when the view differs from the saved settings. Click ... > Save to keep the change.

The ... menu of the report view has these items. Some show only when you have the permission.

Item What it does Show Totals Adds a total row for number columns. Print Prints the table. Toggle Chart Shows a chart. Pick the X axis field, Y axis fields and chart type. Pick Columns Selects the columns to show. Export Downloads the rows (see Export). Setup Auto Email Makes an Auto Email Report that sends this report on a schedule. Save / Save As Save updates this report. It shows for the report owner and Report Managers. Save As makes a new report. Delete Deletes the saved report. User Permissions Opens the User Permissions of the DocType.

docs.title: Run a Query or Script Report
docs.text:
1. Search for the report name in the awesomebar, or open /desk/query-report/<Report Name>.
  2. Set the filters at the top. The report runs again on each change.
  3. Use the Actions button, the icon buttons and the ... menu for more actions.
Item What it does Reload Report (icon button) Runs the report again. Edit Opens the Report document. Documentation Opens the Documentation URL of the report, when set. Print Prints the report. Export Downloads the data. Setup Auto Email Makes an Auto Email Report. Add Column Adds a column from a linked DocType. User Permissions Opens User Permissions for the report DocType. Shows for System Managers. Save Saves your columns and filters as a Custom Report. Shows for Report Managers only. Actions > Create Card Makes a Number Card from a number column. Actions > Set Chart / Add Chart to Dashboard Makes a chart from the report and adds it to a Dashboard.

Related Reports shows other saved versions of the same report.

docs.title: Prepared reports
docs.text:
A prepared report runs in a background job and saves the result. Use it for a report that takes a long time.

  • Turn on Prepared Report (prepared_report) in the Report document.
  • For a Script Report, Frappe turns it on for you when one run takes more than 15 seconds. To stop this, turn on Disable Prepared Report Automation.
  • Timeout (In Seconds) sets the job timeout. The default is 1500 seconds.

When a report is prepared:

  1. Set the filters and click Generate New Report.
  2. Frappe makes a Prepared Report with status Queued. The status changes to Started when a worker picks it up.
  3. When the job ends, the status is Completed or Error. You get a notification with a link to the result.
  4. Click Edit to change the filters, or Rebuild to run it again with the same filters.

To stop a queued or running job, open the Prepared Report and click Cancel Prepared Report. The status becomes Cancelled.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
Export opens a dialog with these options:

Option Default Description File Format Excel Excel or CSV. Export in Background off Makes the file in a background job. CSV Delimiter , CSV only. CSV Quoting Non-numeric Minimal, All, Non-numeric or None. CSV Decimal Separator . CSV only. Shows when CSV Quoting is not Non-numeric.

In the report view, the dialog also asks if you want to export all matching rows when there are more rows than the page shows. Export shows only when you have export permission on the DocType.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
• A user can open a report when they can read its Ref DocType and have one of the roles in its Roles table.
  • Non-standard Query and Script Reports can be saved only by a user with the Script Manager role.
  • Disabled hides the report.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Write Query and Script Reports in an app as files in <module>/report/<report_name>/. See Reports (developer).
  • Run a report from code or the API with frappe.desk.query_report.run(report_name, filters).
  • frappe.core.doctype.prepared_report.prepared_report.make_prepared_report(report_name, filters) queues a prepared report.
  • frappe.desk.query_report.save_report(reference_report, report_name, columns, filters) makes a Custom Report.
  • frappe.desk.reportview.save_report(name, doctype, report_settings) saves a Report Builder report. It checks create permission on Report and read permission on the DocType.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A Report Builder report works on one DocType and its child tables. Use a Query or Script Report for joins.
  • A prepared report shows the result of the last run, not live data. Check the Finished At time.
  • When Administrator saves a new report in developer mode, Frappe sets is_standard to Yes and writes it to the app.

  • Views
  • Dashboards

docs.title: System Administration
docs.text:
Configure the system, take backups and monitor logs and jobs.

Page What it covers System Settings Site-wide settings in System Settings (formats, login, password, email, files, backups, scheduler), plus the basics of Website Settings and Navbar Settings. Backups Take, download, schedule, encrypt and restore site backups with bench and the Download Backups page. Logs and Monitoring Find errors and check site health with Error Log, Activity Log, Access Log, Scheduled Job Log, RQ Job, RQ Worker, Recorder, System Health Report, System Console and Log Settings.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: A site backup has up to four files: the database dump, the public files, the private files, and a copy of site_config.json. You take backups with bench backup and restore them with bench restore. System Managers can download recent database backups from the desk. Take a backup before each update, and schedule regular backups on production servers.

docs.title: Backup files
docs.text:
Frappe saves backups in sites/<site>/private/backups/. You can change the folder with the backup_path key in site_config.json. File names start with the date and time and the site name, with dots changed to underscores:

File Example name Database 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-database.sql.gz Site config 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-site_config_backup.json Public files 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-files.tar Private files 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-private-files.tar
  • Partial backups (with includes or excludes) have -partial before -database.
  • Encrypted backups have -enc before the extension.
  • With --compress, file archives are .tgz.

docs.title: Take a backup
docs.text:
# database and site config only
bench --site frappe.localhost backup

# also public and private files
bench --site frappe.localhost backup --with-files

# all sites of the bench
bench --site all backup

Options of bench backup:

Option Description --with-files Also back up public and private files. --compress Compress the file archives (.tgz). -i, --include, --only DocTypes to back up, separated by commas. -e, --exclude DocTypes to leave out, separated by commas. --backup-path Folder for all backup files. --backup-path-db, --backup-path-files, --backup-path-private-files, --backup-path-conf Path for each file. --ignore-backup-conf Ignore the includes and excludes in site config. --verbose Print more output.

bench backup prints a summary with the path and size of each file.

docs.title: Includes and excludes in site config
docs.text:
To always back up only some DocTypes, or to always leave some out, add a backup key to site_config.json:

{
 "backup": {
  "excludes": ["Version", "Deleted Document"]
 }
}

Use includes for the other case. Frappe skips DocTypes that have no table, without a message. This applies to site config and to --include and --exclude. If no included DocType has a table, Frappe takes a full database backup.

docs.title: Schedule backups
docs.text:
Frappe does not take backups on its own. On a server, use the bench CLI to add a cron job:

bench setup backups

This adds a cron job that runs bench --verbose --site all backup every 6 hours and writes to logs/backup.log.

docs.title: Old backups
docs.text:
Frappe deletes old backups in two ways:

  • Each new backup first deletes all files in the backup folder that are older than 23 hours. Set keep_backups_for_hours in site config to change this.
  • An hourly job (frappe.desk.page.backups.backups.delete_downloadable_backups) keeps the newest Number of Backups (backup_limit, default 3) sets and deletes the rest.

Copy backups to another server or storage if you need to keep them longer.

docs.title: Download backups from the desk
docs.text:
1. Go to Download Backups (/desk/backups). You need the System Manager role.
  2. Click a backup to download the database file.

The page shows the newest database backups, up to Number of Backups. Each download makes an Access Log entry. The buttons are:

Button What it does Set Number of Backups Opens System Settings at Number of Backups. Download Files Backup Queues a backup with files on the long queue. Frappe emails you the download links when it is done. Get Backup Encryption Key Shows the encryption key after you confirm your password.

docs.title: Encrypt backups
docs.text:
1. Go to System Settings > Backups.
  2. Set Encrypt Backups (encrypt_backup).
  3. Save.

Frappe then encrypts the database and file archives with gpg. The gpg program must be installed on the server. The key is backup_encryption_key in site_config.json. Frappe creates it the first time it needs it. Store the key outside the server. Without it, you cannot restore an encrypted backup.

docs.title: Restore a backup
docs.text:
Warning

bench restore replaces the whole database of the site. Take a backup of the site first.

bench --site frappe.localhost restore \
  sites/frappe.localhost/private/backups/20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-database.sql.gz \
  --with-public-files sites/frappe.localhost/private/backups/20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-files.tar \
  --with-private-files sites/frappe.localhost/private/backups/20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-private-files.tar
  • If the path does not exist, bench restore also looks in sites/<site>/private/backups and in the bench folder.
  • For an encrypted file, Frappe uses --encryption-key. Without it, Frappe uses backup_encryption_key in site config. If the site has no key, Frappe makes a new one, and the decryption fails.
  • --admin-password sets the Administrator password after the restore.
  • On MariaDB, Frappe asks you to confirm when the backup comes from a newer version of Frappe. --force skips this check and the SQL file validation.
  • Run bench --site <site> migrate after a restore from an older version.

A partial backup cannot be restored with bench restore. Use bench --site <site> partial-restore <file>. It restores only the tables in the file, into the existing site.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.backups import new_backup

odb = new_backup(ignore_files=True, force=True)
print(odb.backup_path_db)
  • frappe.utils.backups.new_backup(...) takes a backup and returns the BackupGenerator. Without force=True, it reuses a complete backup set (database, files, private files and config) from the last 6 hours if one exists.
  • frappe.utils.backups.fetch_latest_backups() returns the paths of the latest backups. It needs System Manager.
  • Site config keys: backup, backup_path, keep_backups_for_hours and backup_encryption_key. See Site Config reference.

docs.title: Logs and Monitoring
docs.text: Frappe records errors, logins, data access, scheduled job runs and background jobs in log DocTypes. Use them to find out why something failed, who did what, and whether workers and the scheduler run. Use the Recorder and the System Health Report to look at performance and the state of the site. Most of these DocTypes need the System Manager role.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: DocType Route What it records Error Log /desk/error-log Unhandled exceptions and errors logged by code. Activity Log /desk/activity-log Login, logout and impersonation. Access Log /desk/access-log Exports, printed documents, report views, private file and backup downloads. Scheduled Job Log /desk/scheduled-job-log One row per run of a scheduled job. API Request Log /desk/api-request-log API calls, if Log API Requests is set in System Settings. RQ Job /desk/rq-job Background jobs in Redis queues. RQ Worker /desk/rq-worker Background workers that run now. Recorder /desk/recorder Requests and jobs with their SQL queries, while recording is on. System Health Report /desk/system-health-report A live summary of workers, scheduler, database, cache, email and errors.

docs.title: Error Log
docs.text:
Frappe adds an Error Log for each unhandled exception in a request or a background job. Code can also add one with frappe.log_error.

Label Fieldname Description Title method Short description, often the last line of the traceback. Error error Full traceback. Reference DocType / Reference Name reference_doctype, reference_name The document the error is about, if known. Seen seen Set when a user opens the log. The list shows "Seen" or "Not Seen". Trace ID trace_id ID of the request or job. Fingerprint fingerprint Hash of the stack. The same error has the same fingerprint.

The form shows how often the error occurred, first seen, last seen and a 30-day chart. Use Show Similar Errors to list logs with the same fingerprint, and Open reference document to open the document.

Some errors are queued in Redis first, for example during read-only requests. The job frappe.deferred_insert.save_to_db saves them every 15 minutes. Clear Error Logs in the list menu deletes all Error Logs.

docs.title: Activity Log and Access Log
docs.text:
Activity Log has Operation (operation: Login, Logout or Impersonate), Status (status), User, IP Address and Subject. Failed logins also show here. Use it to audit who logged in and from where.

Access Log has User, Export From, Reference Document, Report Name, Filters, File Type, Method and Timestamp. Use it to see who exported or printed data.

docs.title: Scheduled Job Log
docs.text: Each run of a scheduled job adds a row with Scheduled Job (scheduled_job_type), Status (Scheduled, Complete or Failed) and Details (the traceback if it failed). Open the Scheduled Job Type to see the frequency and the last run. See Scheduler.

docs.title: RQ Job and RQ Worker
docs.text:
RQ Job and RQ Worker are virtual DocTypes. They read the jobs and workers from Redis. Nothing is saved in the database.

RQ Job fields: Job ID, Job Name, Queue (default, short or long), Status (queued, started, finished, failed, deferred, scheduled or canceled), Timeout, Time Taken, Arguments and Exception.

  • The list shows "Scheduler: Active" or "Scheduler: Inactive". If inactive, use Actions > Enable Scheduler.
  • Actions > Remove Failed Jobs deletes all failed jobs of the site.
  • On a job with status started or queued, Force Stop job stops it.

RQ Worker shows Queue(s), Status, Current Job ID, Successful Job Count, Failed Job Count, Last Heartbeat and Utilization %. If the list is empty, no worker runs. See Background Jobs.

docs.title: Recorder
docs.text:
The Recorder captures web requests and background jobs with their SQL queries, timings, call stacks and EXPLAIN output. Only Administrator can use it.

  1. Go to Recorder (/desk/recorder).
  2. Click Start.
  3. Set the options and click Start Recording.
  4. Do the slow action in another tab.
  5. Click Stop.
  6. Open a row to see its queries.

Option Default Description Record Web Requests / Request path filter on, / Records requests whose path starts with the filter. Record Background Jobs / Background Jobs filter on, empty Records jobs whose name matches the filter. Empty records all. Record SQL queries on Generate EXPLAIN for SQL queries on Capture callstack of SQL queries on Capture document lifecycle timeline on Times each controller method and doc_events handler. Run cProfile off Adds Python profile output. It is slow.

Recording stops on its own after 10 minutes. On a recorded request, Suggest Optimizations proposes database indexes, and Add Indexes adds the ones you select. Use Clear to delete all recordings. Export and Import in the menu move recordings between sites.

From the command line, use bench --site <site> start-recording and bench --site <site> stop-recording.

docs.title: System Health Report
docs.text:
Open System Health Report (/desk/system-health-report). Frappe builds the report each time you open it. It does not save it.

Section What it shows Background Jobs Number of workers, pending jobs per queue, worker use. Background Jobs Check runs a test job and shows its status. Scheduler Scheduler Status, the oldest job that did not run, and failing scheduled jobs of the last 7 days. Database Database type and version, storage use, largest tables. MariaDB Variables Buffer pool size and binary logging. Cache Number of Redis keys and memory use. Realtime (SocketIO) SocketIO Ping Check (Pass or Fail) and the transport mode. File Storage and Backups Size of public and private files, number and size of backups on the server. Users Total users, new users and failed logins in the last 30 days, active sessions. Emails Outgoing, pending, failed, handled and unhandled emails. Errors Error count of the last day and the top errors.

docs.title: System Console
docs.text:
System Console (/desk/system-console) runs Python or SQL on the site from the desk. Only Administrator has access.

  • Type Python runs the code in the same restricted environment as Server Scripts. It needs server_script_enabled in common_site_config.json. See Server and Client Scripts.
  • Type SQL runs only read queries: SELECT, EXPLAIN, and WITH on MariaDB. Queries that read __Auth are rejected.
  • Frappe rolls back all changes unless Commit is set.
  • Each run adds a Console Log with the script and whether it committed.
  • Show Processlist lists the running database queries.

docs.title: Log Settings and cleanup
docs.text:
Log Settings (/desk/log-settings) sets how long Frappe keeps each log. Each row in Logs to Clear has Log DocType and Clear Logs After (days). A daily job deletes older rows. Defaults come from the default_log_clearing_doctypes hook, for example:

Log DocType Days Error Log 14 Scheduled Job Log 7 Email Queue 30 Activity Log 90 API Request Log 90

To shrink a very large log table at once, use the CLI. It first backs up the table, unless you add --no-backup. Then it copies recent rows to a new table and swaps the tables:

bench --site frappe.localhost clear-log-table --doctype "Scheduled Job Log" --days 30

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
try:
    process_sample_order(order)
except Exception:
    frappe.log_error(title="Sample Order sync failed", reference_doctype="Sample Order", reference_name=order.name)
  • frappe.log_error(title=None, message=None, reference_doctype=None, reference_name=None, *, defer_insert=False) saves the current traceback if you do not pass message. It returns the Error Log document.
  • To make your own log DocType clearable, add a static method clear_old_logs(days) to its controller, and add it to the hook:
# sample_app/hooks.py
default_log_clearing_doctypes = {
    "Sample Sync Log": 30,
}
  • The Recorder API is in frappe/recorder.py (frappe.recorder.start, stop, get, delete). See Performance.

docs.text:

  • Performance

docs.title: System Settings
docs.text:
System Settings is a Single DocType with the site-wide settings: language, time zone, date and number formats, login and password rules, email, file uploads, backups and the scheduler. Only the System Manager role can open it. Go to /desk/system-settings. Changes apply to all users after you save.

The form has these tabs: Details, Login, Password, Email, Files, App, Display, Backups, Advanced and AI Agents. The tables below list the main fields of each tab. Field labels are as shown in the form.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
The hidden field Application Name (app_name, default Frappe) is also stored here. Set the name for the login page in Website Settings.

Label Fieldname Default Description Country country Country of the site. Language language Default language. Time Zone time_zone System time zone. Currency currency Default display currency. Enable Onboarding enable_onboarding 0 Shows onboarding steps. Disable Document Sharing disable_document_sharing 0 Nobody can share documents. Date Format date_format For example dd-mm-yyyy or yyyy-mm-dd. Time Format time_format HH:mm:ss HH:mm:ss or HH:mm. Number Format number_format For example #,###.## or #.###,##. Use Number Format from Currency use_number_format_from_currency 0 Uses the number format of the currency. First Day of the Week first_day_of_the_week Sunday Used in date pickers and calendars. Float Precision float_precision Decimal places for Float fields. Currency Precision currency_precision If empty, it comes from the number format. Rounding Method rounding_method Banker's Rounding (legacy) Also Banker's Rounding or Commercial Rounding. Apply Strict User Permissions apply_strict_user_permissions 0 See User Permissions. Show External Link Warning show_external_link_warning Never Never, Ask or Always.

docs.title: Login and Password
docs.text:
The Login tab has session, login method, brute force and two-factor settings. The Password tab has the password policy. See Users and Roles for the full tables. Main fields:

  • Session Expiry (idle timeout) (session_expiry), default 170:00. It must be in the format hh:mm.
  • Enable Two Factor Auth (enable_two_factor_auth). When you turn it on, Frappe sets two-factor authentication on the role All.
  • Enable Password Policy (enable_password_policy), default on, with Minimum Password Score (minimum_password_score), default 2.

docs.title: Email
docs.text: Label Fieldname Default Description Email Footer Address email_footer_address Your organization name and address in the footer. Email Retry Limit email_retry_limit 3 Send attempts before an email fails. Disable Standard Email Footer disable_standard_email_footer 0 Include Web View Link in Email attach_view_link 1 Store Attached PDF Document store_attached_pdf_document 1 Saves the PDF on the Communication. Welcome Email Template / Reset Password Template welcome_email_template, reset_password_template Custom Email Template for these emails.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Label Fieldname Default Description Max File Size (MB) max_file_size Upload size limit. Allowed File Extensions allowed_file_extensions One extension per line. Empty allows all. Allow Guests to Upload Files allow_guests_to_upload_files 0 For example for web forms. Strip EXIF tags from uploaded images strip_exif_metadata_from_uploaded_images 1 Only allow System Managers to upload public files only_allow_system_managers_to_upload_public_files 0

docs.title: App and Display
docs.text:
• Default App (default_app): the app that opens after login. A user can override it on the User form.
  • Dashboards (dashboards), default Insights. Selects how standard dashboards that ship an Insights version open: Insights or Classic. Without the Insights app, they open classic.
  • Hide Empty Read-Only Fields (hide_empty_read_only_fields), default on.
  • Disable System Update Notification and Disable Change Log Notification.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
Label Fieldname Default Description Number of Backups backup_limit 3 Backups to keep. Older ones are deleted. Minimum 1. Encrypt Backups encrypt_backup 0 Encrypts new backups with gpg.

See Backups.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
Label Fieldname Default Description Max Report Rows max_report_rows 100000 Rows the report view can show. Enable Scheduled Jobs enable_scheduler 0 Runs scheduled jobs only if set. The field is hidden in the form. Run Jobs only Daily if Inactive For (Days) dormant_days 4 Runs jobs once a day on inactive sites. 0 turns this off. Submission Queue Timeout submission_queue_timeout 600 Seconds. Maximum 3600. Show Full Error and Allow Reporting of Issues to the Developer allow_error_traceback 1 Shows tracebacks to users. Link Field Results Limit link_field_results_limit 10 Maximum 50. Log API Requests log_api_requests 0 Saves API calls in API Request Log.

Turn the scheduler on or off with bench --site <site> enable-scheduler and bench --site <site> disable-scheduler. If disable_scheduler is set in site_config.json, the scheduler does not run, whatever the setting.

docs.title: AI Agents
docs.text: Enable MCP (enable_mcp, default on), Server Name (server_name) and Agent Instructions (agent_instructions) configure the MCP server. See MCP and Discovery.

docs.title: Website Settings
docs.text:
Website Settings (/desk/website-settings) controls the public website. Basic fields:

Label Fieldname Default Description Home Page home_page Route of the website home page. Title Prefix title_prefix Added to the title of each web page. App Name app_name Frappe Name on the login page. Disable signups disable_signup 1 Turns off self sign-up on the login page. App Logo app_logo Logo on the login page. Brand Image / FavIcon banner_image, favicon Brand in the navbar and the browser icon. Footer Items footer_items Links in the footer. Robots.txt robots_txt Content of /robots.txt.

See Website for the other settings.

docs.title: Navbar Settings
docs.text:
Navbar Settings (/desk/navbar-settings) controls the desk navbar.

Label Fieldname Description Application Logo app_logo Logo in the desk. The app_logo of Website Settings takes priority. Settings Dropdown settings_dropdown Items in the user menu. Help Dropdown help_dropdown Items in the help menu. Announcement Widget announcement_widget Text shown above the desk. Set Widget Color and Is Dismissible.

Each Navbar Item has Item Label, Item Type (Route, Action or Separator), Route or Action, Hidden and Condition. Standard items come from the standard_navbar_items and standard_help_items hooks. bench migrate syncs them. Use Hidden to hide one.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
frappe.get_system_settings("enable_scheduler")         # cached for the request
frappe.db.get_single_value("System Settings", "date_format")
frappe.db.set_single_value("System Settings", "enable_scheduler", 1)
  • frappe.get_system_settings(key) reads from a client cache and caches the document on frappe.local for the request.
  • When you save System Settings, Frappe also saves each changed value as a global default (frappe.db.set_default).
  • To set values when your app is installed, use an after_install hook.
  • Site config keys, such as disable_scheduler, are in Configuration.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Disable Username/Password Login fails unless a Social Login Key, LDAP or Login with email link is enabled. This prevents a lockout.
  • Turning on Enable Two Factor Auth affects all users through the role All.
  • Enable Scheduled Jobs is off by default. The setup wizard turns it on. If it is off, scheduled jobs, such as the email queue, do not run.
